MEASURED 2026-09-02 during the dwm-oyo.2 close-out, under maintainer Ruling 17-B recorded on dwm-oyo.3. Two independent read-only agents plus two fresh adversaries; the verdict survived attack and was strengthened.

WHAT IS TRUE. Seven-day Plan 02 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-07-seven-day-flow-02-calendar-contacts-schedule-hospital.md) was procedurally superseded into the 2026-08-11 amendment Plan 03 by amendment roadmap line 79, which states that Plan 03 owns the same Bead, namely dwm-oyo.3. That reconciliation is real and no bead is missing for the slot. But Plan 03 does not own the same SCOPE: across its 1654 lines it contains ZERO occurrences of seven-day-flow-02, calendar, echo, read-as-acceptance or SevenDayCalendar, and ten of the fourteen Plan 02 Create-paths do not exist at HEAD 646f49e5.

THE FOUR UNOWNED SUBJECTS.
1. The fixed seven-day calendar owner. Plan 02 Task 1 orders one pure SevenDayCalendar owning ORDINARY_BY_DAY and SOLO_BY_DAY. It does not exist; the literals are still duplicated live in scripts/data/DataCatalog.gd:21-37 and autoload/GameState.gd, whose line 38 labels itself an embedded mirror of DataCatalog. All 18 Task-1 and Task-2 identifiers return zero files.
2. Ordinary-message echo obligations. req.contact.echo is registered with empty evidence. Note the correction that must not be re-derived: the shipped echo id is derived from the ATOM id and enforced at DialogicEntryManifest.gd:562-566 as IDS_MANIFEST_ECHO_BINDING_INVALID (DEVIATION-4 Ruling G), NOT from the reply id as Plan 02 line 132 mandates. Plan 01 froze a different law rather than partially satisfying this one.
3. Both P-L group windows. Plan 02 Task 3 two-window state did not ship: AVAILABLE_UNOPENED exists only inside GROUP_OPEN_STATES, solos still use AVAILABLE (ContactInvitationState.gd:321, :409, :533), and migrate_v2_to_current and group_actions_by_window return zero files repo-wide. The failure is silent, not loud: _classify_pl_window still runs on day 6 (:1612-1616) and with a RESOLVED group carried from D2 returns the private_offscreen outcome at :667, and the group_not_inactive refusal guard at :529 has ZERO test fixtures repo-wide.
4. The Day-7 echo drain. req.run.day7_echo_drain (prompt_docs/requirements/run_lifecycle.md:15, described at :48-50) has no claimant; pending_echoes returns zero files across .gd and .tscn; and DAY_7_STAGES at scripts/domain/run/DayResolutionPlan.gd:20-23 is exactly lock_day, validate_schedule, close_invitations_run_end, validate_day7_provenance, checkpoint_day7_provenance, with no echo-drain stage.

THE ORTHOGONAL PROOF OF ORPHANHOOD, INDEPENDENT OF KEYWORD SCANNING. req.contact.fixed_calendar and req.contact.echo (prompt_docs/requirements/contacts_invitations.md:10-11) and req.run.day7_echo_drain (run_lifecycle.md:15) all carry implementation_evidence empty and verification_evidence empty, and a JSON scan of all 88 live beads finds ZERO claiming any of the three - while sibling requirements from the same files ARE claimed, req.invitation.solo by four beads and req.contact.history_watermark by dwm-p2r.6.

WHY THIS IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT MERELY TIDY-UP. Amendment Plan 03 line 892 states that deferred_pair_request is null outside the registered Day-2/Day-6 P-L window, consuming exactly the window vocabulary subject 3 was written to produce, from a producer that does not exist. So the gap is a live input to the very plan that superseded it.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It does not authorize executing seven-day Plan 02; amendment roadmap line 79 names executing both plans as forbidden duplication. It does not reopen or re-scope dwm-oyo.3. It carries no runtime implementation authority: the seven-day design implementation_authorization_scope is seven_day_flow_phase_01_dwm_oyo_2_only and that grant is spent.

title: The reply-line closure law is never armed: configure_line_registry has zero production callers, so mark_line_visited admits any line id
description:
The reply-line closure law exists, is fully tested at its seam, and is NEVER ARMED in
production. Measured at 646f49e56249442209872123b1bb98f60b9f57c7 on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed in
worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-resealed during the Phase 01 Verification Gate run
(DEVIATION-16 on dwm-oyo.2). No byte was written; the tree was 0 dirty paths before and after.

THE CHAIN, EACH LINK MEASURED.

1. autoload/ProfileManager.gd:417 declares configure_line_registry(registry). A git grep for that
   name across every tracked .gd returns the one declaration plus 35 hits, and every single one of
   the 35 is inside tests/unit/test_dialogic_identity_registries.gd. ZERO production call sites.

2. autoload/ProfileManager.gd:438-440 is the whole admission predicate:
       func _line_registry_admits(line_id: String) -> bool:
           if _line_registry_fingerprint.is_empty(): return true
           return _line_registry_index.has(line_id)
   _line_registry_fingerprint is written only by configure_line_registry. Because nothing calls
   that in production, the fingerprint is permanently empty and the predicate is unconditionally
   true.

3. autoload/ProfileManager.gd:161-163 mark_line_visited therefore refuses ONLY the empty string.
   Its named refusal &"unregistered_line_id" at :163 is unreachable in production.

4. The live caller is autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:467, inside request_skip_step. It takes line_id
   from _runtime_adapter.current_line_id() at :456 and checks only is_empty() at :457. There is no
   registry check anywhere upstream of the write.

SEVERITY QUALIFIER, ALSO MEASURED, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN PATCHED IN PLACE.
current_line_id is defined in exactly one place tree-wide: tests/integration/test_dialogic_skip.gd:44,
a test fake. No production adapter defines it, and it is absent from
scripts/narrative/DialogicRuntimeAdapter.gd:18 REQUIRED_METHODS. So request_skip_step cannot complete
in production at all today, which is precisely what dwm-3an records. This is therefore a LATENT
fail-open, not a live one: it arms itself the moment dwm-3an is closed. Whoever closes dwm-3an must
close this in the same breath, or fixing the skip path will silently ship a global visited-history
writer that accepts any nonempty string as a line id.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG. The law itself is real and well proven at its seam.
tests/unit/test_dialogic_identity_registries.gd carries the command envelope, block closure, record
shape, empty and non-string line_id refusals, duplicate and widening refusals, and the
unregistered-id refusal. Measured GREEN this session at 2 scripts / 46 tests / 46 passing / 169
asserts, run together with tests/unit/test_art_manifest.gd. The defect is wiring, not law.

COST, PRICED AGAINST THE SEALS RATHER THAN ESTIMATED. Arming it needs one production call site plus
a fingerprint source (the parsed ids document already reaches ProfileManager's seam in the tests).
If the call site lands in autoload/DialogicBridge.gd, note that
evidence/phase_2r/handoff/desktop_contract.json binds that path from LIVE bytes with subject_commit
null, so ANY byte change to the bridge - a comment included - forces that handoff re-seal on its own.
evidence/phase_2r/schedule/gate.json does NOT re-seal: it hashes the bridge from its own frozen
subject commit 2bd24eb2ad0c4d76337cf0868257b77a7be666c0, not from the working tree. If the call site
lands only in autoload/ProfileManager.gd, no handoff contract binds that path and there is no
re-seal at all. Prefer the ProfileManager-only shape for that reason.

RELATED. dwm-3an (request_skip_step calls current_line_id, which the production adapter does not
define) is the blocker that keeps this latent. dwm-oyo.2 Phase 01 Verification Gate item 5 is the
gate line this sits under; its other four nouns - signals, atoms, visuals, context identity - were
measured closed and pinned in the same pass, and context's remaining field-level gap is dwm-n3h.

title: Specification 12.3 frozen-context field law is unenforced: frozen_context is a bare four-key Dictionary
description:
Measured during Phase 01 Task 7 (dwm-oyo.2, DEVIATION-15). Recorded because Ruling 14-C owes a bead for anything measured as genuinely unowned, and this is the one item of DEVIATION-14's DEFECT 9 that no plan claims.

WHAT THE SPECIFICATION REQUIRES. docs/design/2026-08-07-seven-day-dialogic-flow-design.md section 12.3 (line 1022) enumerates the frozen presentation context's applicable fields, gives a role-family table of REQUIRED frozen fields for eleven entry roles - ordinary message, solo invitation offer, group contact/offer, consequence/follow-up, solo pre-challenge, solo post-challenge, Hospital, pair pre-challenge scene, pair post-challenge scene, solo ending/exceptional step, P-L ending/Observer step and Alone step - and states the operative law: "Every concrete manifest entry expands the applicable row into one exact discriminated schema; it may add only fields explicitly enumerated for that entry and rejects every undeclared field." It also closes ending_form as an eleven-value union and forbids a sentinel friend, a fake Neutral attitude or a dummy tier for P-L and Alone.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ENFORCED, MEASURED AT autoload/DialogicBridge.gd. _PLAYBACK_CONTEXT_KEYS is exactly four - expected_stage, playback_id, role, transaction_id - and _exact_context_keys enforces only that exact four-key set on both start_entry and resume_entry. The record in data/manifests/dialogic_entries.json carries context_schema_id (for example context.ordinary_message.contact.ordinary.lavinia.day1.v1) and role, but NOTHING resolves context_schema_id to a schema and nothing validates a context against it. So the eleven role-family field lists, the per-entry discriminated schemas, the ending_form union and the no-sentinel rules are all unrepresented in executable code.

WHY IT IS NOT TASK 7's. Task 7's plan block cites 10.1, 12.4 and 14.3-14.4; 12.3 reaches it only transitively through the Task 5 bridge surface, and Task 7 types the prepared plan's frozen_context as a bare Dictionary exactly as the plan's own six-field block specifies. Task 7 DOES now type-guard the checkpoint's primitives at the restore trust boundary and refuses undeclared extra keys at the top level, but that closes the six-field plan shape, not the frozen context's interior.

WHY IT MATTERS. A restore or a start currently accepts any four-key context whose values are Strings, so a context that is wrong for its role - missing the fields its role family requires, or carrying fields its entry never declared - reaches Dialogic as a valid frozen context. DTL may branch on the frozen presentation context, so an unvalidated interior is a presentation-correctness hole, not merely a schema tidiness one.

LIKELY SHAPE OF THE WORK. Resolve context_schema_id through a published schema per entry, validate the frozen context against it inside the bridge's existing seam, and refuse with a named code. Note the blast radius before starting: DialogicBridge.gd is sha256-bound in evidence/phase_2r/handoff/desktop_contract.json and is one of the five ABSENT_SURFACE_SYMBOLS files, so every new column-zero public entry is +1 against the frozen tooling assert figure (14396 as of 646f49e56249442209872123b1bb98f60b9f57c7) and a handoff re-seal is owed in the same commit. Widening _PLAYBACK_CONTEXT_KEYS would move the frozen bridge-contract 1/14/14/275 and signal-boundary 1/30/30/244 baselines.
notes: 2026-09-14 read-only audit at047eb091e confirms full12.3 frozen context remains required after per-scene DTL simplification. All137 manifest records have a narrower presentation_signature_schema, but semantic start_entry/resume enforce only four bookkeeping keys; context_schema_id remains an identifier without executable full-field schema. No production start_entry caller exists, so signature-only bridge hardening would not complete playable context delivery. Keep OPEN. Full implementation needs exact per-entry frozen-context schema, production context builders, shared start/resume validation and immutable DTL-facing projection. Preserve per-scene locators and historical seals. No code or manifest changes in this audit; Day7 Auto is the selected independent runtime increment. Externally owned dwm-634 family is excluded.

title: request_skip_step calls current_line_id, which the production adapter does not define
description:

Today the defect is masked: configure_skip_context has no production caller, so the path short-circuits at :457-458 with skip_context_not_configured before ever reaching the adapter call. This matters because it is the entrance that Phase 01 Task 6's visited-line identity law exists to guard, and specification 12.6 forbids exactly this class of identity - IDs are not derived from file path, line number, translated text, or label position.

NOT REPAIRED BY TASK 6. title: Finish current scene-DTL validator diagnostics and CLI testability
description:
Deferred out of Phase 01 Task 3 sub-commit 3A (commit 3c4f28f0b8c5884f337ce32ee4969d8606b9798d). All items share ONE root: the Task 3 dialogic tooling declares laws that nothing reaches or enforces. None is blocking; all were measured, not argued.

PART A, THE THREE RESIDUAL MUTATION SURVIVORS. The final 76-site campaign at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-task3-campaign closed at 73 KILLED / 3 SURVIVED / 0 INVALID. The three survivors are G11 (the generator pre-write validation guard), C04 (the CLI per-master validate_file call) and C05 (the CLI non-zero exit branch). All three live inside the _run() of an extends SceneTree tool. Reaching them requires instantiation, and instantiating generate_master_skeletons.gd EXECUTES it and rewrites all eight masters from inside a test run, which is precisely why test_dtl_master_structure.gd preloads the generator and calls its static _build instead. A source-text assertion pinning those control-flow statements was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: this repository's text assertions pin published vocabulary (failure code names, count constants) where a rename must not pass unnoticed, and extending them to arbitrary statements would pin spelling rather than behaviour and read as coverage that does not exist. Both tools ARE exercised end to end by recorded manual runs (DIALOGIC_CONTRACT: PASS masters=8 entries=139 exit 0; GENERATE_MASTERS: OK 8 masters / 139 entries exit 0). Closing this needs a production seam that separates the decision body from the SceneTree entry point, the way _build is already separated, so a test can drive it without executing the tool.

PART B, FIVE FINDINGS FROM THE 3A FRESH REVIEWER, all independently re-confirmed against source by the controller before being recorded.

FINDING 1 SHOULD-FIX, tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd. CAUSAL_LINE and VARIATION_LINE are whitelisted then discarded; their PRESENCE is never required. Each constant appears only at its declaration and at one continue. A master with all 139 CAUSAL INPUT and VARIATION lines deleted validates CLEAN and validate_dialogic_contract.gd exits 0 on it, even though the file header presents the five-line block shape as law. The blank-line-count row of the whitelist is likewise unenforced, and an annotation appearing before the first label is silently swallowed. KNOWN LIMITS records none of this. THE MUTATION CAMPAIGN COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT: a check that does not exist cannot be mutated. Fix: record causal and variation presence in the block dictionary and emit DTL_ANNOTATION_MISSING for each absent one, then raise the count assertion in test_the_validator_rejects_a_block_with_no_annotations from 2 to 4 and assert both new message fragments. If the looseness is instead deliberate, amend KNOWN LIMITS so the header stops overclaiming.

FINDING 2 SHOULD-FIX, DtlStructureValidator.gd _classify. Four of the six sub-terms in the two hazard predicates are unreachable by any fixture; deleting the load-paren disjunct or any of the three call-branch terms survives the whole suite. Only V28 and V29, which got dedicated tests, die. Safety is unaffected because the closed whitelist still refuses the line; only the reported failure code is wrong. Fix: one fixture per uncovered term, each chosen so no other term also matches.

FINDING 3 SHOULD-FIX, tools/dialogic/generate_master_skeletons.gd. The generator opens whatever path the manifest names for WRITE with no containment check, while the read-only CLI has one. Its only guards are partition size 8 and total 139; DialogicEntryManifest.validate_document requires only a non-absolute res:// string, and the schema constrains locators.en.path to minLength 1. A wholesale retarget of one master group satisfies every guard, so the generator would overwrite the named file, project.godot included, and report success. The tool that WRITES has strictly weaker containment than the tool that only READS. Fix: share the CLI check before FileAccess.open, refusing unless the path begins with res://dialogic/timelines/en/ and the remainder holds no slash. THIS IS THE ITEM MOST WORTH DOING FIRST: three lines, plus one fixture, plus one campaign site.

FINDING 4 NOTE, tools/dialogic/validate_dialogic_contract.gd. begins_with(MASTER_DIR) accepts a legacy subdirectory path, so the CLI cannot detect the one manifest defect that would break the Ruling O partition it exists to protect: a master retargeted under a subdirectory would be collected by TimelineManifestBuilder and take timelines.json from 61 to 62. Fix as in Finding 3, same check.

FINDING 6 NOTE, DtlStructureValidator.gd. DTL_TRAILING_FALLTHROUGH reports lines.size(), always one past the last real line because every master ends with a newline. Fix: report the offending label's own line, consistent with every other block-scoped failure.

TWO FINDINGS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED HERE. Finding 5 (all 27 assert_string_contains calls pass a description into GUT's match_case parameter) changes no behaviour, since a non-empty String is truthy and match_case defaults true, and it is a pre-existing repo-wide pattern also present in test_day_resolution_coordinator.gd; it belongs to a GUT-usage sweep, not to this bead. Finding 7 (tools/evidence/capture_phase_2r_baseline.ps1 counts 69 English timelines where the sealed baseline.json records 61) is a SECOND unscoped walker of exactly the Ruling O shape, but baseline.json is immutable and digest-sealed by test_legacy_disposition.gd and nothing re-runs the script; record it wherever that script is next revived.

VERIFICATION OWED WHEN THIS IS CLOSED. Per the DEVIATION-4 CARRY-FORWARD, every law added here needs a campaign site that reaches it. Re-run the Task 3 harness at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-task3-campaign with new sites for each new branch, and re-run sites G11, C04 and C05 to prove they now die: a fixture without a site proves only that the suite is green. Then both frozen gates (25 scripts / 474 tests / 473 passing / 1 pending / 0 failing / 14396 asserts, and DOC_VALIDATION PASS packets=16 design_authorities=4 agent_workflow=1) and the four affected suites.

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
FINDING ADDED FROM THE PHASE 01 TASK 6 SESSION, 2026-09-01. This bead already owns the DtlStructureValidator findings, and DEVIATION-11 Ruling B keeps Task 6 out of that file entirely so this bead stays whole as a single batched campaign. Here is one more validator defect, measured at source at HEAD 2673550e47271fa9a638a7b821effc6a9096b9b7, that belongs with the rest.

THE DTL PREFIX ESCAPE. tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd is described as a closed whitelist, and it is - but it is closed over LINE SHAPES, not over LINE CONTENT. Three of its seven accept branches are begins_with prefix matches rather than exact equality: :129 LABEL_PREFIX which is the six characters label followed by a space, :155 PURPOSE_PREFIX, and :159 SIGNALS_PREFIX. Everything after those prefixes is arbitrary text that is accepted at that stage and never reaches _classify at :164.

CONSEQUENCE. A line reading label res://art/portraits/lavinia.png CONTAINS res:// yet can never produce DTL_DYNAMIC_RESOURCE_PATH; it is swallowed at :129 and degrades to DTL_UNREGISTERED_LABEL, a different code carrying a different message. Worse, the :156 and :160 guards read if current is not the empty string, so a line reading # PURPOSE: res://art/... outside any open label block produces NO failure of any code at all.

WHY IT IS ENTIRELY UNTESTED. All six hazard-injection tests in tests/unit/test_dtl_master_structure.gd mutate VALIDATOR.CAUSAL_LINE, which is the one EXACT-EQUALITY branch. No test drives a hazard through a prefix branch, so this escape has never been exercised in either direction.

TWO SMALLER MEASUREMENTS FROM THE SAME PASS, both about the whitelist and code disagreeing. First, :126 accepts a blank line anywhere and any number of times, while the file's own doc comment at :21 claims exactly one between blocks - the code enforces neither the count nor the placement. Second, :125 does not strip_edges before the whitelist while _classify does strip at :241, so the string return followed by one trailing space fails the exact compare at :145, falls through to _classify, is stripped there, matches no hazard, and is reported as DTL_DIALOGUE_LINE.

CONTEXT WORTH KEEPING. The zero-occurrence property still holds today: across all 70 .dtl files in the repository the tokens background, character, portrait, res://, user:// and load( occur zero times, case-sensitive and case-insensitive, proven with positive controls establishing the greps reached every file. So this is a latent hole, not a live breach. The file's KNOWN LIMITS block at :50-54 says a future authored mode must RE-SCOPE the validator rather than relax it in place, which is the right frame for fixing this.

HOUSEKEEPING, CORRECTED. This bead's DESCRIPTION still cites 14388 asserts. The true frozen tooling figure has been 14394 since Task 5, re-measured exact 2026-09-01. The acceptance criteria inherit the stale number by reference to both frozen gates rather than stating it, so only the description needs the edit.

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
PART C, A FOURTH VALIDATOR FINDING: THE PREFIX-MATCH ESCAPE. Recorded 2026-09-01 by the Phase 01 Task 6 implementation session, which is the third bead DEVIATION-12 carry-forward item 6 owes. This is Ruling B territory and was deliberately NOT folded into Task 6; it belongs here, with the rest of the DtlStructureValidator work, so dwm-oyo.2.2 stays one batched campaign.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd is a CLOSED whitelist, but the whitelist is closed over LINE SHAPES, not over LINE CONTENT. Three of its seven accept branches are begins_with PREFIX matches, not exact-equality matches: :129 "label ", :155 "# PURPOSE: " and :159 "# ALLOWED SIGNALS: ". A line is swallowed by whichever prefix branch matches it and never reaches _classify at :239, which is the only place DTL_DYNAMIC_RESOURCE_PATH (:82, emitted :244-246) can fire.

THE TWO CONCRETE ESCAPES.
1. A line reading `label res://art/portraits/lavinia.png` CONTAINS res:// yet is consumed by the :129 label branch. It degrades to DTL_UNREGISTERED_LABEL - a DIFFERENT code with a DIFFERENT message from the one the hazard deserves. The refusal still happens, so this is a mislabelled refusal rather than an accepted hazard, but the code a consumer sees is wrong.
2. A `# PURPOSE: res://...` line sitting OUTSIDE any open label block produces NO failure of any code at all, because :156 and :160 guard on `if current != ""`. That is a genuine acceptance, not a mislabelling.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. All six hazard-injection tests in tests/unit/test_dtl_master_structure.gd mutate VALIDATOR.CAUSAL_LINE, which is the one EXACT-EQUALITY branch. The prefix branches are therefore entirely untested against content hazards. The escape is invisible to the current suite by construction.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT. Measured across all 70 tracked .dtl files (the 69 under dialogic/ plus tests/fixtures/dialogic/phase2r_contract_fixture.dtl): background, character, portrait, res://, user:// and load( occur ZERO times, case-sensitive and case-insensitive, by three independent methods, with positive controls proving the greps reached every file (git grep -o -F -- ':' returns 1016 matches; git grep -I -l returns all 70, so none is skipped as binary). No shipped master exercises the escape today.

WHAT CLOSING IT REQUIRES. The content check must run BEFORE the shape whitelist, or each prefix branch must re-check its remainder, and the KNOWN LIMITS block at :50-54 says a future authored mode must RE-SCOPE the validator rather than relax it in place - so this is a re-scope, not a patch. Note the cost: tests/unit/test_dtl_master_structure.gd is one of the four suites inside the FROZEN 4/242/242/11631 baseline, so any new validator law moves it and needs the amendment re-seal recipe. That is exactly why DEVIATION-11 Ruling B ring-fenced this file out of Task 6 and left it byte-identical, preserving the 76-site Task 3 campaign proof over those exact bytes.

TASK 6 CONFIRMED THE RING-FENCE HELD: tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd is byte-identical at the Task 6 commit, and the four-suite baseline re-measured EXACT at 4/242/242/11631 after the edit.

title: Ending label spelling diverges from spec: observation vs observer
description:
Two live ending labels in the English Dialogic tree carry a suffix the seven-day design never uses as
an ending identity. At HEAD the tree has ending.lavinia.observation and ending.priscilla.observation,
but docs/design/2026-08-07-seven-day-dialogic-flow-design.md section 13.8 names the stable identity
observer and enumerates the callable entries ending.lavinia.observer.full, ending.lavinia.observer.residue,
ending.priscilla.observer.full and ending.priscilla.observer.residue. The word observation appears in
the spec only as a common noun (pure-observation board, full-observation line), never as an ending id;
observer appears 49 times as the identity.

PROVENANCE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. Commit 9114351031ffd874b7079e6df12da915c4d27808 (Sun Aug 9 2026,
feat(dialogic): register exact timeline and narrative manifests) renamed all three retired .true labels
in one pass: ending.sylvia.true became ending.sylvia.special, which IS the spec word and maps cleanly
to ending.sylvia.special.full and .residue; ending.lavinia.true and ending.priscilla.true became
.observation, which is not. So the rename was internally inconsistent within a single commit, and only
two of the three labels drifted off the spec vocabulary.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY. The maintainer ruled on 2026-08-27 that the seven-day Phase 01 frozen
migration manifest (data/migrations/dialogic_61_to_8.json, dwm-oyo.2 Task 1) maps these two labels to
their .observer entries and records legacy_name_is_non_canonical on those rows, so the inventory keeps
the information rather than losing it. That ruling deliberately does NOT edit the .dtl files: Phase 01
Task 1 is inspect-only for the legacy tree, and a Global Constraint keeps the 61 legacy DTL and UID
files intact until Plan 06 proves the physical cutover.

WHAT REMAINS TO DO, AND WHEN. At the physical cutover the label written into the eight master timelines
must be the spec identity observer, not observation. Whoever performs the cutover must not carry the
legacy spelling forward. The frozen manifest rows are the record of the intended correspondence.

NOT AFFECTED, DO NOT CONFLATE. The three retired ending.*.true labels are a different matter and are
already correctly recorded with status rejected and never aliased to an Observer entry, per the plan
and per DEVIATION-2 on dwm-oyo.2. Bare label ending.priscilla_lavinia is also a different matter: it
names none of its three ending ids (.sweet, .dark, .observer) and stays unmapped by the same ruling.
close_reason: Resolved through replacement per-scene DTL architecture: six canonical observer.full/residue locators resolve and production playback accepts them. Fresh test_dtl_master_structure.gd passed7/7 tests178assertions (ihm-scene-layout-audit-20260912.log). Registered legacy observation resources remain for compatibility; no mass rename is claimed. Audit: docs/agent/2026-09-12-backlog-reconciliation.md

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
MEASURED CONSEQUENCE OF THIS DIVERGENCE, recorded 2026-09-01 by the Phase 01 Verification Gate run
on dwm-oyo.2 (DEVIATION-16). This adds a measurement, not a new decision; the 2026-08-27 ruling this
issue records is untouched.

At 646f49e56249442209872123b1bb98f60b9f57c7 the observation-vs-observer divergence has a concrete,
countable effect that this issue's description does not yet state: it leaves THREE of the thirteen
registered ending IDs accepted by NO production function anywhere in the tree.

THE ARITHMETIC, measured against the shipped manifests rather than inferred.
data/manifests/dialogic_ids.json declares ending_id_count 13 and thirteen ending_ids. Of those
thirteen, EIGHT are also registered entry_ids in data/manifests/dialogic_entries.json and so resolve
through DialogicEntryManifest.resolve_entry. The remaining five do not, and return ok:false with
ENTRY_MANIFEST_UNKNOWN_ENTRY - the same code reserved for a stranger:

    ending.alone                     accepted instead by data/manifests/endings.json (11 records)
    ending.sylvia.special            accepted instead by data/manifests/endings.json
    ending.lavinia.observer          accepted by NOTHING
    ending.priscilla.observer        accepted by NOTHING
    ending.priscilla_lavinia.observer  accepted by NOTHING

So across the union of both ID-taking production seams - resolve_entry over the 139 entries and
DialogicBridge._start_playback over the 11 endings.json records - the clause "13 ending IDs validate"
measures 10/13, and 8/13 at the entry seam alone.

WHY THIS ISSUE OWNS IT RATHER THAN A NEW BEAD. The first two orphans are exactly the two labels this
issue already names: the legacy tree spells them .observation while the spec identity is .observer,
so the .observer form has no physical label to resolve to until the Plan 06 cutover writes it. The
third, ending.priscilla_lavinia.observer, falls under this issue's own closing paragraph, which
already sets aside bare ending.priscilla_lavinia as naming none of its three ending ids and staying
unmapped by the same ruling.

WHAT THE CUTOVER OWNER SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS. Writing the spec identity .observer into the eight
masters at cutover is not only a spelling correction; it is what makes three currently-unresolvable
registered ending IDs resolvable. Ruling 16-A on dwm-oyo.2 deliberately left the reading of gate
item 1's second clause - registry-block validation versus per-ID acceptance - to whoever owns this
cutover, precisely so that the ruling is made on this evidence rather than re-derived. Both
measurements are recorded on dwm-oyo.2 under DEVIATION-16.

title: Re-seal the dwm-p2r.16 identity issuer boundary after legitimate source evolution
description:

Two have legitimately drifted since the recorded boundary_commit 86b125484fd09b86efc7e5925cd4c9b28f9e39c4: scripts/application/desktop/DesktopIdentityNonceIssuer.gd (drifted at b9206a685, the Task-8 fix that returned the frozen action-consequence contract and added the action_consequence child kind) and scripts/data/DataCatalog.gd (drifted at 69cf694e0, refactor(contacts) one canonical friend roster). The plan's own text says later consumers should validate the .16 boundary against its NAMED COMMIT-TREE bytes plus ancestry rather than pinning evolved current files - the historical validation passes; only the current-byte pin fails. The controller ruled this non-fatal during Task 6 (recorded on dwm-p2r.32.5 addendum rule 4). It has simply never been re-sealed after the evolution.

ACCEPTANCE. Either re-seal the v1 record's current-source expectations against a new named commit (preserving the immutable historical record rather than overwriting it, per the plan's never-overwrite-v1 law), or formally retire the DWM_REQUIRE_CURRENT_P2R16_BOUNDARY current-byte mode as superseded by the historical check, and record the decision so the gate is green in its literal form.

Delivered in commit aedbc9168792078336d67e6c5a811acc182f25ee (sole child of fa4ba16b7, via Invoke-ExactPathCommit): validate_boundary_record loses the require_current mode; the boundary test gains a retirement pin asserting the record validates while bound sources genuinely drift (2 of 7 today: issuer at b9206a685, DataCatalog at 69cf694e0). The v1 record is byte-untouched - never-overwrite-v1 holds trivially. title: A replayed substage completion never reports duplicate_transaction
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-context review of the dwm-p2r.20 fix plan.

THE GAP. The duplicate scan in prepare_completion walks active_resolution_plan[stages] and never
stage[substages]. A replayed SUBSTAGE completion therefore never reports duplicate: true. It falls
through to complete_active_stage, where _complete_record returns duplicate_transaction_conflict on a
differing receipt and a bare ok on an identical one.

CONSEQUENCE. A replayed substage returns stage_completed with a FRESH checkpoint rather than
duplicate_transaction. Every other seam in the coordinator is replay-idempotent and reports the
duplicate; substages silently are not. Present in the production port and mirrored in
tests/support/FakeDayResolutionStatePort.gd, so the fake would lie to any test that exercised it.

SCOPE NOTE. The dwm-p2r.20 tests deliberately avoid the duplicate path for exactly this reason.

ACCEPTANCE. The duplicate scan considers substages, so a replayed substage completion reports
duplicate_transaction and writes no second checkpoint, matching stage behaviour. RED proves the
current fall-through first. Fix the fake in the same change, or the unit suite cannot hold the claim.

REFERENCE. docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-20-p2r20-substage-contract-through-the-route-door.md

title: Carry contacts through the Minesweeper round transaction so group activation can commit
description:
Discovered 2026-08-17 while closing dwm-p2r.9 Step 2.5 coverage gaps on branch codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed.

Plan 06 Task 2 Step 2.4 item 7 requires the completion transaction to pass exact before/after round counts to ContactInvitationState so that only a 2->3 transition on Day 2/6 activates the group offer. That cannot happen today, and the cause is structural rather than a missing call.

GameState._SAVE_WHITELIST (autoload/GameState.gd:78-95) does NOT include the 'contacts' section. Consequences, both independently fatal:

1. GameStateMinesweeperPort._detached_clone() rebuilds its clone via reset_game() + apply_save_dict(to_save_dict()). Because to_save_dict() omits contacts, the clone always starts from DEFAULT contacts, so prepare_activate_group_after_round()'s 'both pair solos unread and AVAILABLE' predicate fails with missing_solo and never activates.
2. The port's candidate is exactly clone.to_save_dict(), which also omits contacts, so even a successful activation could never reach the committed candidate.

Verified empirically by probe on 2026-08-17: 'to_save_dict has contacts? false', 'candidate has contacts? false', receipt.group_activation_transaction_id = null, live group_action state after prepare = INACTIVE.

Therefore the hardcoded receipt values group_activation_transaction_id=null and message_transaction_ids=[] in GameStateMinesweeperPort.prepare_complete are TRUTHFUL for the current candidate surface. This is not a receipt-reporting bug; do not 'fix' it by populating those fields while contacts remain outside the transaction, or the receipt will claim a state change that was never committed.

Note that GameState._bridge_maybe_activate_group() (autoload/GameState.gd:750-763) IS correctly implemented and DOES activate on the live object with transaction id 'gactivate:day<N>'. Only the Minesweeper round transaction path cannot reach it.

dwm-p2r.9 deliberately closed without this. The plan's own rule is that only fake ports exercise this transport in .9, and the coordinator/dating contract coverage added on 2026-08-17 (139/139 gate) stands independently.
design: Widen the Minesweeper round transaction's candidate/commit/rollback surface to carry the contacts section alongside gameplay, mirroring how capture_live_run_state() and capture_restore_backup() already treat contacts as a sibling section. Then populate CompletionReceipt.group_activation_transaction_id and message_transaction_ids from the transactions the domain actually recorded, by diffing contacts.transaction_receipts on the clone and classifying new entries by their 'kind' field ('activate_group' vs 'offer_solo') rather than re-deriving the activation rule in the port. Changing the committed candidate shape touches RunSnapshotSchema and the save/restore path, so expect migration and snapshot-validation work; it also invalidates evidence/phase_2r/handoff/minesweeper_contract.json and requires regenerating both handoff artifacts and their seven-record ledger.
acceptance_criteria: Completing the third app round on an eligible Day 2 (and Day 6) commits group_action state AVAILABLE_UNOPENED with a null inviter_id and history_generated=false, and the CompletionReceipt reports the matching gactivate transaction id. Transitions 1->2 and 3->4, non-window days, and ineligible or already-read solo offers all commit no activation and report null. Dating rounds never activate the group under any transition. Both handoff artifacts and the command ledger are regenerated and validate clean.

THE QUESTION. No bead was titled for Phase 02; the epic reads 00, 01, 03, 03, 04, 05, 06; and this bead description says to execute the reconciled Plan 03 under the amendment specification. PRE-FLIGHT MEASURED THIS SESSION, NOT ASSUMED. Worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-resealed is on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed at e1285c5e559fc1f42a77796ac925d3fc935d4042, the exact Task 1 final head, with git status --short -uall EMPTY (not even the previously noted untracked .superpowers/). Counting sections 13.1 through 13.7 bullet by bullet gives 10 / 24 / 20 / 13 / 13 / 24 / 17 = 121 day entries, and the 13.8 table expands to 18 presentation entries, total 139. The Phase 01 Verification Gate independently names the per-file counts 10/24/20/13/13/24/17/18. The two agree exactly, so the manifest day field is assertable against the gate.

RULING 1, TEST FILE NAME. The plan orders Create tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd, but that file ALREADY EXISTS at 107 lines and binds the LEGACY contract: data/manifests/timelines.json 61 records with 24 placeholder and 37 draft, data/manifests/endings.json 11 records including the non-canonical ending.lavinia.observation, and DialogicTimelineCatalog path resolution. Global Constraint keeps the 61 legacy DTL and UID files until Plan 06 proves the physical cutover, so that coverage is still live and must not be destroyed. DISPOSITION: the new Task 2 suite is tests/unit/test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd. The legacy suite stays byte-untouched. Both are named in the Task 2 GREEN command. Divergence is one filename against plan prose and nothing else.

RULING 2, THE 18 REPLY IDS. Spec 12.8 enumerates them as reply.ordinary.lavinia.day1.a and siblings. The plan Task 2 table writes reply.contact.ordinary.lavinia.day1.a, namespaced under the entry id to match its own line. and atom. columns. They cannot both be THE 18 because 12.2 declares the manifest closed. DISPOSITION: the SPEC form wins. Register reply.ordinary.FRIEND.dayN.a|b|c, exactly 18 complete strings, zero shorthand. This follows the Task 1 precedent that every registered id appears VERBATIM in the design spec with zero invented ids. The plan table remains authoritative for its OTHER two columns, the authoritative reply line ids and the guaranteed Day 7 fallback atom ids, because the spec enumerates no counterpart for either. Plan-prose divergence to be filed as its own bead alongside dwm-ihm.

RULING 3, WHAT A SCHEMA FILE CAN AND CANNOT ENFORCE. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: scripts/validation/JsonSchemaValidator.gd implements exactly ten keywords - type, const, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minItems, minLength, uniqueItems. Everything else is SILENTLY IGNORED, including pattern, oneOf, allOf, maxItems, dollar-ref, propertyNames, minimum, maximum and if/then/else. The keyword pattern appears in this repo only under schemas/evidence/, which is validated by the SEPARATE tools/evidence/EvidenceValidator.gd, never by JsonSchemaValidator. So the Task 2 checkbox demanding the schema reject duplicate locator pairs, absolute OS paths, non-res paths, and labels unequal to their registered semantic entry is NOT EXPRESSIBLE in schemas/manifests/*.schema.json. DISPOSITION: split the contract. The schema file carries only what the validator truly enforces. DialogicEntryManifest.validate_document carries the four remaining laws as named failure codes. The suite proves each code individually, each is mutation-killed individually, and one extra test asserts that the SCHEMA ALONE does not catch them, so a later agent cannot delete a code law believing the schema still covers it. This follows the CLOSEOUT_PATH_TRAVERSAL precedent from dwm-p2r.10, where a schema character class provably could not exclude what the law had to reject. Writing an inert pattern keyword into a manifest schema is FORBIDDEN by this ruling.

RULING 4, THE NARRATIVE VARIABLES MODIFY IS DEFERRED, NOT DROPPED. MEASURED: tools/dialogic/validate_manifests.gd regenerates data/manifests/narrative_variables.json every run from a hardcoded literal of schema_version 1 with an empty variables array, and writes it through CanonicalJsonWriter, so any hand edit is silently reverted on the next generation pass. That file is also read by scripts/domain/run/RunSnapshotSchema._registered_narrative_variables, which gates every GameState narrative-variable write, and RunSnapshotSchema.gd is SHA-256 source-bound in two evidence contracts, evidence/phase_2r/schedule/gate.json and evidence/phase_2r/handoff/desktop_contract.json. Separately, neither spec section 9 nor 12 nor any Task 2 checkbox names one concrete narrative variable to add; the only obligation is the Task 3 bullet that no unregistered variable exists, and structural mode authors none. DISPOSITION: Task 2 leaves narrative_variables.json BYTE-UNTOUCHED and records that structural mode registers zero narrative variables, so the closed registry is correctly empty. Task 2 therefore touches NINE files, not ten. The Modify lands in whichever later task first needs a variable, and when it does it MUST also change the generator literal in tools/dialogic/validate_manifests.gd in the same commit or the edit will not survive.

RULING 5, THREE ENTRIES HAVE NO ROW IN SPEC 12.3. opening.day1 and tutorial.desktop_day1 from 13.1 and echo.fallback.day7 from 13.7 are callable entries with no role-family row, yet 12.3 requires every concrete entry to expand an applicable row. DISPOSITION: three distinct roles with minimal exact fields. opening and tutorial are presentation-only, required frozen fields exactly entry and day, allowed_signals exactly history.line.witness. echo_fallback requires entry, day, and the due-echo ids with their registered presentation atom ids, honouring 11.1 which states the entry receives the immutable remaining pending-echo list and drains it oldest first; allowed_signals are history.line.witness and message.echo.satisfy. Recorded as three named gaps in 12.3, not as an invention.

RULING 6, THE THREE DAY 7 ENDING INVITATIONS. contact.invitation.ending.priscilla.day7.offer and its lavinia and sylvia siblings are boardless ENDING invitations: 11.1 makes eligibility a durable-tier test, makes reading the invitation its scripted acceptance, and makes Done commit at most one personal ending destination. Reusing solo_invitation_offer was rejected because Plan 05 would then have to re-parse the entry id string to tell a boardless ending invitation from a date invitation, which 12.2 forbids.

CONTROLLER RULING, NOT ESCALATED, stated so no implementer has to guess it. The manifest day field means the OWNING MASTER FILE, per 12.2 which says role and owning day/ending layer. A Day 1 carryover such as contact.invitation.solo.priscilla.day1.nevermind lives in day_2.dtl and therefore records day 2; its source day is frozen CONTEXT, per the 12.3 Consequence/follow-up row which asks for display day and source invitation separately. Under this reading the per-day tallies are exactly 10/24/20/13/13/24/17 with day null on all 18 ending entries, matching the Phase 01 Verification Gate figure. ending_id is non-null on exactly those 18 and null on all 121 others.

DIGEST IMPACT: NONE. No plan bytes and no design bytes change under any of these six rulings, so every row of the roadmap Plan Digest Manifest and every implementation_plan_sha256 remain exact.

DEVIATION-4 (Phase 01 Task 2 sub-commit 2B: atom home, stage vocabulary, line namespace, suite file, and echo binding). Maintainer-decided 2026-08-27 on measured evidence, batched as a pre-flight plan review before any implementer was dispatched. Five rulings, all binding on 2B and on every task that consumes data/manifests/dialogic_ids.json.

PRE-FLIGHT MEASURED THIS SESSION, NOT ASSUMED. Worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-resealed is on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed at 26c26eacf0bf166a0d71900e3e19f37ed022c7df, the exact sub-commit 2A final head, with git status --short -uall EMPTY, the staged index empty, and .godot/phase2r_tests/ empty. Re-verified independently from the committed bytes: dialogic_entries.json carries exactly 13 distinct ending ids and exactly 11 distinct ending forms, matching specification 13.8 and the 12.3 union; data/migrations/dialogic_61_to_8.json carries exactly 3 retired_labels; scripts/validation/JsonSchemaValidator.gd still implements exactly the ten keywords DEVIATION-3 Ruling 3 named, so Ruling 3 continues to bind and no inert constraint keyword may enter the new schema. Annotation keys are not constraints: the 2A schema uses description and dollar-schema freely and that precedent stands.

CROSS-CHECK THAT SETTLED THE PAIR ATOMS WITHOUT A GUESS. The plan mandates exactly four full Priscilla-Lavinia observation atoms - atom.pair.day2.group.full, atom.pair.day2.twofriends.full, atom.pair.day6.group.full, atom.pair.day6.twofriends.full. The four pair_post_challenge_scene entries in the 2A manifest are dating.group.priscilla_lavinia.day2.post_challenge, dating.twofriends.priscilla_lavinia.day2.post_challenge and their day6 siblings, and they are EXACTLY the four entries 2A granted pair.combination.witness. The mapping is therefore 1:1 and forced, not chosen, and it gives 2B a hard cross-registry invariant: an entry holds pair.combination.witness if and only if it owns exactly one pair_full_observation atom.

RULING C, WHAT AN ATOM RECORD DECLARES. Ruling B already fixed that a namespace is a declared HOME and never a string prefix. 2B hits the next layer: the plan says the six ordinary rows own exactly three line IDs and three Day-7 fallback atom IDs apiece, and the 2A docstring records atom.echo.lavinia.day1.reply.a.fallback.day7 as belonging to contact.ordinary.lavinia.day1, yet 12.8 makes message.echo.satisfy valid only for a registered echo atom actually presented in the current entry, and 11.1 makes echo.fallback.day7 the entry that presents the remaining pending echoes. Owner and presenter genuinely differ for those 18 atoms. DISPOSITION: each atom record declares BOTH owning_entry_id and presented_in_entry_ids. owning_entry_id is the ordinary entry, exactly as the plan and the committed 2A docstring say, so nothing already committed is contradicted. presented_in_entry_ids is echo.fallback.day7 for the 18 guaranteed fallback atoms and the same post_challenge entry for the 4 pair atoms. validate_atom_id resolves ownership from the record and accepts entry_id when it is either the declared owner or a declared presentation site, reporting which; it MUST NEVER require a string prefix. Reading the owner as the presenter was rejected because it contradicts both the plan bullet and committed bytes; accepting only the owner was rejected because it would leave echo.fallback.day7 unable to validate the very atoms 11.1 obliges it to present.

RULING D, THE STAGE VOCABULARY IS DERIVED FROM SPEC PHRASES, NOT INVENTED. MEASURED: the specification never enumerates a stage vocabulary anywhere. 12.2 asks only for an allowed source stage, 12.8 describes each in prose in its Valid source column, 12.4 mentions a registered continuation stage and 14.3 says every entry declares resumable stages. Task 1 precedent is that every registered id appears VERBATIM in the specification. DISPOSITION: close the vocabulary at FOUR values, each snake-cased from the specification own phrase rather than from a new word - awaiting_reply from 12.8 while awaiting reply; current_entry from 12.8 in the current entry; after_full_observation_atom from 12.8 after its full Perfect/Solved observation atom; registered_dating_scene_action from 12.5 at its registered canonical dating-scene action. Each signal record declares allowed_source_stages and validate_signal rejects a stage outside it with a named code. The assignment is message.reply.commit awaiting_reply, history.line.witness current_entry, message.echo.satisfy current_entry, observer.evidence.commit registered_dating_scene_action, pair.combination.witness after_full_observation_atom. A single shared stage was rejected because it would make the plan-named stage parameter inert and unreachable by any mutation, which is precisely the dead-law pattern the sub-commit 2A survivor S08 lesson forbids. Deferring the vocabulary was rejected because it ships a plan-named parameter with no law. The tokens are the divergence and are recorded here; the phrases they come from are spec text.

RULING E, LINE IDS RESOLVE BY DECLARED HOME AND THE PREFIX IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A LAW. MEASURED: all 18 plan-mandated line ids DO begin with their owning entry line_namespace, while 0 of the 22 plan-mandated atom ids begin with theirs. DISPOSITION: validate_line_id resolves ownership from the record declared owning_entry_id only, uniformly with Ruling B, and enforces no string shape. The suite separately asserts that all 18 line ids begin with their owner line_namespace as a CHANGE DETECTOR, explicitly not a specification proof - the same status sub-commit 2A gave ROLE_COUNTS. Enforcing the prefix in production was rejected because it would bind every future content line 12.8 says is added alongside its content, and would enforce 12.2 compatible namespaces asymmetrically against atoms. Asserting nothing was rejected because a silent respelling of all 18 line ids would then pass every test.

RULING F, 2B OWNS ITS OWN SUITE. tests/unit/test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd is 1924 lines after 2A. DISPOSITION: 2B tests land in a new tests/unit/test_dialogic_ids_manifest.gd, and BOTH suites are named in the Task 2 GREEN command - the pattern DEVIATION-3 Ruling 1 already established for two coexisting suites. The 2A suite stays byte-untouched except where a 2B production change provably requires it. This is a second filename divergence from plan prose and nothing else. Rationale: the ids registry is a distinct artifact with its own schema and its own load path, one fresh reviewer can hold it whole, and Task 1 likewise owns its own suite.

RULING G, ECHO IDS BIND ON THE ATOM RECORD. Specification 9.3 states verbatim that every authored echo binds its echo_id to one stable presentation_atom_id, and the 12.8 message.echo.satisfy payload carries both fields, yet the 2B dispatch list names no echo-id registry and no echo_id string is enumerated anywhere. DISPOSITION: each of the 18 echo_fallback atom records carries echo_id, derived from the plan OWN mandated atom id by stripping the atom. prefix and the .fallback.day7 suffix, so atom.echo.lavinia.day1.reply.a.fallback.day7 binds echo.lavinia.day1.reply.a. validate_signal then enforces the 9.3 binding directly: for message.echo.satisfy the payload echo_id and presentation_atom_id must be the registered pair, so a mismatched pair fails closed. This expands the artifact by one field beyond the dispatch list; the strings are plan-derived rather than invented. A separate echo_ids block was rejected as an S08-shaped split of one binding across two places, and registering nothing was rejected because it would ship a payload field the closed manifest could not fail closed on, against 12.2.

CONTROLLER RULINGS, NOT ESCALATED, stated so no implementer has to guess them. (1) The document parameter of validate_signal, validate_line_id and validate_atom_id is the ENTRIES document, uniformly with validate_document and resolve_entry, which is the only reading consistent with the plan using one word for all five signatures. The ids registry is read from disk by a private helper mirroring the 2A _load_schema, and a public validate_ids_document(ids_document) takes the ids document explicitly so every named ids failure code stays fixture-reachable and individually mutation-killable. (2) validate_signal composes rather than duplicates: it checks payload.entry_id equals the entry_id argument, that the entry_id 2A allowed_signals grants signal_id, that the stage is allowed for that signal, that the payload field set is EXACTLY the 12.8 field list with no missing and no extra field, and then delegates line_id to validate_line_id and presentation_atom_id to validate_atom_id. playback_token and receipt_id are runtime-generated, so 2B constrains them to non-empty strings only and says so. (3) reply_id values are validated against the 18 registered reply ids and must belong to the emitting ordinary entry. (4) The three retired ids are registered with reject_on_restore true carried through from Task 1, and resolve_entry gains a distinct retired-entry failure code so a legacy label arriving from a save is refused BY NAME rather than as a generic unknown entry; this is the only 2A behaviour change 2B makes and it is additive over three exact strings.

DIGEST IMPACT: NONE. No plan bytes and no design bytes change under any of these rulings, so every row of the roadmap Plan Digest Manifest and every implementation_plan_sha256 remain exact.

CARRY-FORWARD, THE S08 LESSON RESTATED FOR 2B. Whenever a law is split across the schema and the code, both halves must be independently mutation-killed or one half is deletable in silence. The new schema must therefore have its own pins-its-own-literals test, and every code law the schema provably cannot express must have a test proving the schema alone does not catch it.

comments.text:
TASK 2 SUB-COMMIT 2B MUTATION CAMPAIGN COMPLETE AND FRESH REVIEW COMPLETE. NOTHING IS COMMITTED. HEAD is still 26c26eacf0bf166a0d71900e3e19f37ed022c7df and the working tree is byte-identical to the state the previous session left, SHA-256 verified against the pristine snapshot on all five boundary files.

HARNESS RELOCATED SO A HANDOFF CAN FIND IT. The campaign harness lived in a dead session's scratchpad, one temp-cleanup away from taking the pristine snapshot with it. It now lives at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-2b-campaign, outside every worktree so it can never pollute git status. It holds campaign.py, the five-file pristine/ snapshot with pristine_sha256.json, Run-Campaign.ps1 (the driver), check_empty_blocks.py, patch_broken_mutants.py, analyse.py, BINDING-RULINGS.txt, COMMIT-COMMAND.ps1, and the two result files campaign-results.jsonl and repair-results.jsonl.

THE CAMPAIGN WAS RUN AGAINST THE 2B SUITE ALONE, DELIBERATELY. Both suites together take 174s; test_dialogic_ids_manifest.gd alone takes 44s for 80 tests and 1944 asserts. Eighty-five sites at 174s is over four hours; at 44s it is about seventy minutes. The escalation rule was fixed in advance: any site SURVIVING under the 2B suite would be re-run under both suites before being called a survivor. No survivor needed that escalation for the reason given below. Controller-run baseline attested this session before any mutation: 1 script / 80 tests / 80 passing / 0 failing / 1944 asserts, exit 0.

A CHEAP PRE-FLIGHT THAT SHOULD BECOME STANDARD. Before spending an hour of Godot time, all 85 mutants were applied and reverted WITHOUT running Godot, purely to prove every anchor still matches exactly once. All 85 applied. That costs seconds and would have caught a stale anchor before it cost a run.

THE HARNESS HAD A REAL DEFECT AND IT WAS SILENTLY DESTROYING SIX SITES. Site C06 came back with 52 failing tests, asserts collapsed from 1944 to 1373, and a 10s runtime instead of 40s. The log said: Parse Error: Expected indented block after "for" block, then Failed to load script. The mutation deletes the entire BODY of its enclosing for loop, so the whole production script fails to compile and every test fails for a reason unrelated to the law under test. A mutant that never compiles is NEITHER A KILL NOR A SURVIVOR - it is an INVALID MUTANT, and the law it targets was never exercised at all. Reported as a kill it would have been a false green over a law nobody had tested.

A LOCAL DETECTOR FOUND EVERY INSTANCE WITHOUT GODOT. check_empty_blocks.py applies each code mutant in memory against the pristine snapshot and asks one local question: if the last meaningful line before the edit opens a block, is the first meaningful line after the edit indented strictly deeper? A first attempt keyed on line numbers and produced 26 false positives, because deleting lines shifts every later line and re-flags multi-line function signatures. Keying the question LOCALLY to the edit reduced it to 7. Six were genuine: C06, C11, C12, C13, C32, C33, each deleting the whole body of a for loop. The seventh, C27, is a FALSE POSITIVE verified by hand - its apparent opener is the continuation line of the multi-line validate_signal signature at two tabs while the body is one tab, so the body is not emptied. C27 was independently KILLED in the campaign, which proves empirically that it compiled.

THE SIX WERE REPAIRED AND RE-RUN, AND ALL SIX NOW KILL. The repair keeps the loop structurally intact while still disabling the law, reusing the harness's own existing idiom from C03 and C09: an if false guarding a print of the loop variable, which also keeps the loop variable used. The first patch attempt was REJECTED BY ITS OWN ASSERTION because the anchor for C12 also matched C29 - both entries end with the text percent-signal_id-close-paren. Because the patcher writes only after every anchor validates, campaign.py was left byte-identical rather than half-patched, confirmed by SHA-256 against the untouched original. The second version keys on each unique site key and rewrites only the empty replacement at the end of that entry, and records that campaign.py stores tabs as the two literal characters backslash-t inside a Python string literal, so the replacements must be raw strings or real tabs would be emitted and corrupt the harness.

A CLASSIFICATION RULE THAT WAS WRONG, CORRECTED, AND WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. The driver's live rule treated ANY SCRIPT ERROR line as an anomaly. That conflates two opposite things. Sites C28, C36 and repaired C32 each removed a guard whose absence then crashes a later unguarded dictionary lookup - for example C28 deletes the not-index-has-entry_id guard and validate_signal then dies on Invalid access to property or key on a base object of type Dictionary. Those runs ALSO failed two or more named assertions. That is a STRONG kill, not a harness fault: the crash is the consequence of the disabled law. The corrected rule, applied in analyse.py, is that only Parse Error, Failed to load script, SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED and SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED mean an invalid mutant; a bare SCRIPT ERROR alongside named failing assertions is a kill.

FINAL OBSERVED RESULT, 85 SITES: 80 KILLED, 5 SURVIVED, 0 INVALID REMAINING. Every kill names at least one failing test; the count of kills with no named failing test is zero. Of the 40 schema sites, all 40 are killed, and 34 of them die specifically to test_the_published_ids_schema_pins_its_own_literals, with the remainder to the closes-every-object-level, rejects-every-empty-identifier and rejects-every-unknown-vocabulary-value tests. That is the S08 lesson holding for the schema half across every literal the campaign enumerates. All 5 manifest sites are killed.

THE FIVE SURVIVORS, EACH A NAMED LAW NO MUTATION CAN KILL. Each ran exit 0 at a full 80 passing and 1944 asserts, so each is a clean survivor and not a near miss.
C08 - DialogicEntryManifest.gd around 567, the elif echo_id is not null half of IDS_MANIFEST_ATOM_PARTITION_INVALID, a pair atom that carries an echo id. The production docstring declares both halves of the law; only the echo-atom-without-an-echo-id half has a fixture.
C15 - around 601, the known-has-label_id half of IDS_MANIFEST_RETIRED_ID_INVALID, a retired label that is also a callable entry. The 2B suite header narrows this law to one half while the production header states both.
C17 - around 619, the not-granted-and-owned-is-not-zero direction of IDS_MANIFEST_PAIR_WITNESS_MISMATCH. The existing fixture moves a pair atom onto an entry that DOES grant the witness, so both affected entries land on the other branch.
C18 - around 624, the first IDS_MANIFEST_ORDINARY_TRIPLE_MISMATCH loop, a reply or line or atom owned by an entry that does not grant message.reply.commit. The existing fixture moves a reply onto another ORDINARY entry, so only the tally loop fires.
C40 - _is_retired_label around 831, where return record.get reject_on_restore == true becomes return true.

C40 IS THE MOST INTERESTING SURVIVOR AND IT COLLIDES WITH A CONTROLLER RULING. It is NOT a missing fixture. MEASURED: load_ids_default does not validate, it only checks existence and parses strict JSON; and _is_retired_label reads the registry from IDS_MANIFEST_PATH on disk rather than from an injected document. All three shipped retired records carry reject_on_restore true, so no fixture can distinguish return-true from the real expression without writing a mutated registry to disk. The reject_on_restore condition inside _is_retired_label is therefore unreachable from any fixture BY CONSTRUCTION. DEVIATION-4 controller ruling (1) states the intent explicitly: a public validate_ids_document takes the ids document explicitly so every named ids failure code stays fixture-reachable and individually mutation-killable. _is_retired_label's disk coupling defeats that intent for this one condition. This is a design question, not a test-authoring question.

ONE FRESH READ-ONLY REVIEWER RAN CONCURRENTLY AND INDEPENDENTLY, AND IT CONVERGED. To keep it honest it was NOT given the live worktree, whose five files were transiently holding deliberate defects for the whole hour; it was given its own detached worktree at 26c26eac populated with the pristine bytes and SHA-256 verified identical. It was told not to run Godot, not to write anything, and not to re-derive the registry or re-run gates. It found NO correctness bug: it verified Rulings B, C, D, E and G, the DEVIATION-4 composition ruling, and the 2A suite diff, all clean, and it re-derived Ruling 3's ten-keyword claim from JsonSchemaValidator.gd itself before enumerating all 81 constraint occurrences in the new schema and finding zero inert keywords. Its substantive findings were entirely on the S08 axis, and FOUR OF ITS PREDICTIONS ARE EXACTLY THE CAMPAIGN'S SURVIVORS C08, C15, C17 and C18, predicted by reading before the campaign reached them. Two independent methods agreeing on the same four branches is the strongest evidence either can give.

WHAT ONLY THE REVIEWER COULD SEE, BECAUSE THE CAMPAIGN ENUMERATES NO SITE FOR IT. First, the record-is-object law at DialogicEntryManifest.gd around 499 is a SECOND IDS_MANIFEST_BLOCK_SHAPE law distinct from the block-is-array law at 496. Only the array law has a site, C01, and C01 is killed. The reviewer's reasoning that the record law is uncovered stands untested by measurement: the only BLOCK_SHAPE fixture sets atoms to an empty dictionary, which trips 496 first. Its schema half is uncovered too - the literal test checks items.additionalProperties and items.required but never items.type, and removing items.type makes the node invisible to the open-objects helper rather than flagging it, while additionalProperties keeps working because JsonSchemaValidator keys it off the value being a Dictionary. Each half hides the other. Second, 22 of the schema's 81 constraints are pinned by no test, almost all of them type keywords. Nine of those have real consequence and the mechanism was verified directly against JsonSchemaValidator.gd line 39: minLength is applied ONLY when the value is already a string, so deleting type-string from reply_id lets a numeric reply_id through the schema entirely, and the code then coerces it with str() and accepts it. Third, three type-array keywords on ending_ids, ending_form_union and source_stages are not merely unpinned but UNREACHABLE, because the code's block-is-array check at 496 runs before the schema; likewise allowed_source_stages.items.minLength.

TREE STATE, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED, AFTER EVERYTHING ABOVE. The five boundary files hash exactly to the pre-campaign pristine snapshot. HEAD is 26c26eacf0bf166a0d71900e3e19f37ed022c7df. git status --porcelain -uall UNFILTERED is exactly the six expected paths and nothing else. The staged index is empty. .godot/phase2r_tests/ is EMPTY, so no sandbox leaked across 91 Godot runs. The temporary review worktree was removed so no later agent can read stale bytes from it.

A MAINTAINER DECISION IS NOW REQUIRED AND 2B MUST NOT COMMIT UNTIL IT IS MADE. The DEVIATION-4 CARRY-FORWARD is binding and says: whenever a law is split across the schema and the code, both halves must be independently mutation-killed or one half is deletable in silence. Five named laws currently fail that test, plus the record-is-object law and its schema half, plus nine consequential schema type literals. The 2A precedent is that its S08 survivor was FIXED in a fix wave before the commit, not deferred. Against that, closing all of it expands 2B by roughly five to seven new fixtures, the missing schema literal pins, a decision on the three unreachable type-array keywords, and a design decision on _is_retired_label's disk coupling - and it requires re-running the campaign afterwards, plus new campaign sites for the newly covered laws.

WHAT REMAINS BEFORE 2B CAN COMMIT: the maintainer's scope decision on the five survivors and the reviewer's coverage findings; whatever fix wave that authorises, with a fresh reviewer for it; a re-run campaign; then BOTH frozen gates re-run at the final tree; then Invoke-ExactPathCommit. The exact commit invocation is pre-derived and staged at COMMIT-COMMAND.ps1, checked against the helper's own enforcement: the .uid companion must go in -OptionalPresentStatus with status A, -ExpectedHead must be the full 40 characters, and the message may contain no double quotes and no backticks. The gates were NOT re-run this session because the tree is byte-identical to the tree at which the previous session already ran them; they must be re-run at whatever final tree the decision produces.

comments.author: Siuuuers
comments.text:
DEVIATION-5 (Phase 01 Task 2 sub-commit 2B: S08 coverage closure scope). Maintainer-decided 2026-08-27 on measured evidence, after the completed 85-site mutation campaign and one fresh read-only review had both reported. Five rulings, all binding on the 2B fix wave. This deviation decides SCOPE only; it overturns none of DEVIATION-3, DEVIATION-4, Ruling A or Ruling B, and it changes no plan or design bytes, so every roadmap Plan Digest Manifest row and every implementation_plan_sha256 remain exact.

RULING H, THE FOUR FIXTURE-REACHABLE SURVIVORS ARE CLOSED IN 2B. C08, C15, C17 and C18 each name a law whose second half no mutation can kill, and all four were predicted independently by the fresh reviewer before the campaign reached them. DISPOSITION: the fix wave adds one fixture per branch to tests/unit/test_dialogic_ids_manifest.gd, so that each of these four mutants dies to a NAMED test. Specifically it needs a pair atom that carries an echo id (C08), a retired label that is also a callable entry (C15), a pair atom owned by an entry that does NOT grant pair.combination.witness (C17), and a reply or line or atom owned by an entry that does not grant message.reply.commit (C18) - note that the existing C17 and C18 fixtures fail to reach these branches precisely because they move the record onto an entry that still satisfies the other side of the condition. These are TEST-ONLY additions. No production byte, no schema byte and no data byte changes under this ruling, so the controller's 55-of-55 artifact verification and the 154/154/7626 GREEN both stand unchanged.

RULING I, C40 IS RECORDED AND DEFERRED, NOT CLOSED IN 2B. MEASURED: load_ids_default does not validate, it only checks existence and parses strict JSON; _is_retired_label reads the registry from IDS_MANIFEST_PATH on disk rather than from an injected document; and all three shipped retired records carry reject_on_restore true. The reject_on_restore condition inside _is_retired_label is therefore unreachable from any fixture BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why C40 survives, and it collides with the intent stated in DEVIATION-4 controller ruling (1) that every named ids failure code stay fixture-reachable and individually mutation-killable. DISPOSITION: closing it requires a PRODUCTION seam - _is_retired_label taking an injected registry the way validate_ids_document already takes an injected document - and that is a wider change than an otherwise additive sub-commit should carry. It is deferred to its own bead and MUST be closed by whichever later task first designs that seam. Recorded here so it is a known deferred gap rather than an undiscovered one. Deferring the whole set was rejected because the other four cost only fixtures; closing C40 inside 2B was rejected because a production seam change would widen the blast radius of a sub-commit whose every other change is additive.

RULING J, THE RECORD-IS-OBJECT LAW AND ITS SCHEMA HALF ARE BOTH CLOSED IN 2B. MEASURED by the fresh reviewer and confirmed against the bytes: DialogicEntryManifest.gd carries TWO distinct IDS_MANIFEST_BLOCK_SHAPE laws - the block-is-array law around line 496 and the record-is-object law around line 499 - and only the first has a campaign site, C01, which is killed. The single BLOCK_SHAPE fixture sets a block to an empty dictionary, which trips 496 first, so the record law has no fixture. Its schema half is equally uncovered: the literal test checks items.additionalProperties and items.required but never items.type, the open-objects helper only inspects nodes that already declare type object so deleting it makes the node INVISIBLE rather than flagged, and additionalProperties keeps working because JsonSchemaValidator keys it off the value being a Dictionary. Each half hides the other, which is the exact S08 shape. DISPOSITION: add a fixture that puts a NON-OBJECT record inside a well-formed array block, pin items.type in the schema literal test for all five record blocks, and add both as campaign sites.

RULING K, THE NINE CONSEQUENTIAL SCHEMA TYPE LITERALS ARE PINNED. MEASURED directly against scripts/validation/JsonSchemaValidator.gd: minLength is applied ONLY when the value is already a string. So deleting type string from reply_id lets a numeric reply_id through the schema entirely - no type check runs and minLength is skipped - and the code then coerces it with str() and accepts it. The same holds for line_id, atom_id, presented_in_entry_ids.items, label_id and the three owning_entry_id fields, of which owning_entry_id is the one exception because a non-string owner is still caught as IDS_MANIFEST_UNKNOWN_OWNING_ENTRY. DISPOSITION: pin each of these type literals in test_the_published_ids_schema_pins_its_own_literals and add a campaign site for each, so a silent respelling of an identifier's type cannot pass.

RULING L, THE FOUR UNREACHABLE KEYWORDS ARE KEPT AND COMMENTED, NOT DELETED. The type array keywords on ending_ids, ending_form_union and source_stages, plus allowed_source_stages.items.minLength, are unreachable because the code's own checks run BEFORE the schema - the block-is-array check at 496 and IDS_MANIFEST_SIGNAL_STAGE_INVALID respectively. No mutation can ever kill them. DISPOSITION: KEEP them. They are correct, they cost nothing, and they defend the schema if the code order is ever changed or a check removed. Record them in the schema's own description text as deliberately unreachable belt-and-braces, so a later agent neither mistakes them for live laws nor wastes a campaign site trying to kill them. Deleting them was rejected because it would remove a correct defence purely to satisfy a metric; leaving them undocumented was rejected because the next campaign would enumerate them and report false survivors. NOTE that this ruling deliberately creates a THIRD category beyond killed and survived - documented-unreachable - and any site added for one of these four must be recorded as expected-to-survive with this ruling cited, or omitted entirely.

CAMPAIGN OBLIGATION THAT FALLS OUT OF H, J AND K.
