Line 68 declares HOSPITAL_TIMELINE_ID as hospital.faint and line 910 asserts the live port returns exactly that. The value is produced by scripts/application/run/GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd, where line 1076 sets it and line 1089 reads, verbatim, return timeline_id if DialogicTimelineCatalog.has_timeline_id(timeline_id) else the empty string. Controller-verified by direct grep: hospital.faint occurs ONCE in timelines.json and ZERO times in dialogic_entries.json. Therefore re-pointing has_timeline_id at the 139-entry manifest makes line 1089 return empty, and the frozen gate FAILS. The plan's own Phase 01 Verification Gate independently forbids this: it requires that the 61 old DTL/UID files and the current project.godot registry remain intact pending final cutover.

FINDING 5, ELEVEN LIVE CALL SITES THE TASK 4 FILES LIST OMITS ENTIRELY. The four proposed names has_entry_id, get_required_entry_ids, get_required_master_paths and build_validation_report are unused anywhere in the repo today, but their predecessors are not. has_timeline_id has four production callers: autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:162, scripts/application/run/DatingPresentationPort.gd:248, scripts/application/run/GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd:1089 and scripts/application/run/HospitalPresentationPort.gd:244, plus tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd:73 and :74. get_timeline_path has four production callers: autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:167, :170 and :529, and scripts/application/restore/NarrativeRestoreParticipant.gd:56. get_required_timeline_paths has one, DialogicBridge.gd:214; build_missing_timeline_report has one, DialogicBridge.gd:210; get_record has one, NarrativeRestoreParticipant.gd:39. Three further integration suites consume the injected catalog seam by duck-typed stub without naming the class and break if that interface changes: tests/integration/test_dialogic_restore.gd:19 and :23, tests/integration/test_restore_production_adapters.gd:233 and :237, tests/integration/test_restore_transaction.gd:110 and :112. NOTE THE PLAN'S OWN CONCESSION: it says no production caller may use get_timeline_path by the PLAN 06 gate, not the Plan 01 gate, so the plan itself expects these callers to survive Phase 01.

FINDING 6, THE LOCALE RED CONDITION CONTRADICTS THE SPECIFICATION. Task 4's first bullet demands a RED test proving unsupported locale fabrication FAILS. Specification 14.1 at docs/design/2026-08-07-seven-day-dialogic-flow-design.md lines 1417 to 1425 mandates the opposite: a missing selected-locale path or label falls back ONLY to the exact same semantic label in English, which is a SUCCESS path. DialogicEntryManifest.resolve_entry implements exactly that at lines 382 to 387, returning ok true with used_fallback true. Independently, schemas/manifests/dialogic-entries.schema.json closes locators with additionalProperties false and required en, and top-level locales to the enum en with default_locale const en, so a second locale cannot exist in any schema-valid document and there is no distinguishing input to request. Measured: all 139 records carry exactly one locale key, en. A test asserting ok false would encode a law the specification contradicts.

FINDING 7, TWO OF THE FIVE RED CONDITIONS ARE NOT WRITABLE AGAINST PRODUCTION DATA. Measured across all 139 records: every record carries a non-empty locators.en.label, and there are 139 distinct labels and 139 distinct entry_ids with ZERO duplicates. So the missing-label RED and the duplicate-label RED cannot be driven by the shipped manifest and require fabricated document fixtures. By contrast the arbitrary-suffix RED and the retired-.true RED ARE writable against real production data: an unregistered string reaches ENTRY_MANIFEST_UNKNOWN_ENTRY at DialogicEntryManifest.gd:362, and the three shipped retired_ids records in data/manifests/dialogic_ids.json, all carrying reject_on_restore true, reach ENTRY_MANIFEST_RETIRED_ENTRY at :359.

FINDING 8, THE INTEGRATION-TEST BULLET IS NOT SATISFIABLE IN TASK 4. Plan line 261 orders replacing the integration test's external start_timeline_path() call with a registered semantic fixture entry. That call is at tests/integration/test_profile_reset_consumers.gd:145 and is the ONLY start_timeline_path call site in the entire .gd tree outside the definition at autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:180. It targets res://dialogic/timelines/en/contacts/lavinia_day1.dtl, whose id contact.lavinia.day1 is one of the 27 orphans. It is also LOAD-BEARING: it is what makes Dialogic emit event_handled so the step-order assertion at :149 can fire. Controller-verified: every master begins with a comment line then a bare return on line 2, so a path-only start of a master returns immediately and fires no event, silently voiding the :149 assertion; and Specification 4.1 separately forbids the bridge ever starting a merged file at its beginning. A correct replacement therefore needs a LABEL-AWARE start, which is Task 5's deliverable, not Task 4's.

THE FIVE RULINGS, ALL RATIFIED BY THE MAINTAINER THIS SESSION.

RULING U, REPLACE BECOMES ADD, AND THE 61-ID SURFACE SURVIVES TASK 4. Task 4 ADDS the five-method entry-vocabulary surface alongside the existing timeline-vocabulary surface. It does NOT remove or re-point has_timeline_id, get_record, get_path_for_id, get_required_timeline_ids, get_required_timeline_paths or build_missing_timeline_report. get_timeline_path is MARKED deprecated in comment only and keeps resolving through timelines.json; re-pointing it to get_entry is DEFERRED to the task that migrates its last caller, which is Task 5 for the three DialogicBridge sites and Task 7 for NarrativeRestoreParticipant. Justification is measured, not stylistic: Finding 4 proves the literal re-point breaks the frozen gate through hospital.faint, the Phase 01 Verification Gate independently requires the legacy registry stay intact pending cutover, the Task Interface Map assigns the bridge to Task 5, and the plan's own get_timeline_path bullet names the PLAN 06 gate as the deadline. This is the fourth instance of the Replace-becomes-Add pattern already ruled on three times: DEVIATION-3 Ruling 1, DEVIATION-4 Ruling F, and DEVIATION-7 Rulings N and Q. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: a union lookup that tries dialogic_entries.json and falls back to timelines.json would keep everything green with no deferral, but it re-introduces exactly the permissive resolution Specification 12.2 lines 1018 to 1020 orders closed, that an absent ID fails closed and unknown suffixes do not resolve through permissive pattern parsing.

RULING V, BULLET 2 IS RECORDED AS ALREADY-SATISFIED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT SKIPPED. Findings 1 and 2 establish that the three named helpers do not exist and that has_timeline_id is already exact. Task 4 adds NO new work for that bullet and, critically, does NOT weaken, relocate or delete tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd:65 to :69, the existing test that pins the three names as absent. Recording it satisfied is what keeps the next reader from concluding the bullet was quietly dropped.

RULING W, THE LOCALE RED IS RESTATED TO MATCH SPECIFICATION 14.1. RED condition (e) becomes: get_entry(entry_id, non-en locale) SUCCEEDS, returns the exact English path and label, sets used_fallback true, and NEVER manufactures a non-English path; and get_required_master_paths(non-en locale) returns exactly the 8 English master paths. The plan text is recorded as defective and the specification is authoritative, the same disposition DEVIATION-3 Ruling 3 established. The catalog's existing SUPPORTED_LOCALES of en and its header comment that language selection never manufactures zh_CN or zh_HK paths are consistent with this and stay.

RULING X, THE SUITES SPLIT BY VOCABULARY AND THE OLD SUITE STAYS BYTE-UNTOUCHED. tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd keeps owning the legacy 61-id surface, including its 61-record and 24/37 status assertions, its three-helper-absence pins, its ending.sylvia and dating.solo.sylvia.day3.pre_challenge resolution assertions, and its 11-ending RETIRED_ENDING_IDS check. The new tests/unit/test_dialogic_timeline_catalog.gd owns ONLY the new 139-entry surface. This is not one contract split across two files; under Ruling U there are genuinely two vocabularies, and each gets one suite. test_timeline_manifest.gd is therefore NOT added to Task 4's file set.

RULING Y, THE INTEGRATION TEST DEFERS TO TASK 5 AS A RECORDED CARRY-FORWARD. Per Finding 8, tests/integration/test_profile_reset_consumers.gd is DROPPED from Task 4's file set and stays byte-untouched. The replacement requires a label-aware start that only Task 5 delivers, and Task 5 already owns start_timeline_path's retirement in its own checklist. CARRY-FORWARD, BINDING ON TASK 5: when Task 5 retires start_timeline_path it MUST replace the call at test_profile_reset_consumers.gd:145 with a label-aware semantic start, and it must preserve the event_handled emission that the step-order assertion at :149 depends on. A substitution that does not start real playback silently voids that assertion, which is this repository's documented recurring defect, a test that names a law but never reaches it.

FOUR CONTROLLER RULINGS, NOT ESCALATED, STATED SO NO IMPLEMENTER GUESSES.
(a) THE MISSING-LABEL AND DUPLICATE-LABEL REDS ARE FIXTURE-DRIVEN THROUGH THE INJECTED-DOCUMENT FORM. Per Finding 7 they cannot be driven by the shipped manifest. They are written against fabricated documents passed to the injected-document API, DialogicEntryManifest.validate_document(document) and resolve_entry(document, entry_id, locale), which already take a document parameter. This is the same fixture-reachability discipline DEVIATION-5 Ruling H established, and it is what makes them mutation-killable rather than a law that names itself and is never reached.
(b) THE RETIRED-LABEL SEAM STAYS SHUT. Task 4 asserts ENTRY_MANIFEST_RETIRED_ENTRY through the delegated public API and touches NEITHER _is_retired_label NOR load_ids_default. Measured: the retired-.true RED is fully satisfiable with ZERO edits to DialogicEntryManifest.gd, because all three shipped retired_ids records already carry reject_on_restore true and resolve_entry:358 already reaches them. What dwm-oyo.2.1 owns is strictly the OTHER outcome, making the reject_on_restore false branch fixture-reachable, which no Task 4 bullet mentions and no Task 4 test needs. C40 stays with dwm-oyo.2.1.
(c) THE NEW SUITE SHIPS WITH ITS .uid COMPANION. Every tracked .gd in this repo has one and the catalog's own is uid://dkockipv0hqpb; a new suite without one reproduces the defect commit 43df2d43f exists solely to repair. Generate it with the --import path already proven twice, and guard it with a project.godot SHA-256 check before and after, since project.godot is sealed to f24d9af7... in both handoff contracts.
(d) get_entry OWNS ITS OWN DOCUMENT CACHING, behind the catalog's existing _ensure() and _records static-cache pattern at lines 43 to 45, calling DialogicEntryManifest.load_default() and validate_document(). Three of the five demanded methods are NOT delegation and must be written fresh, because the manifest exposes no equivalent: get_required_entry_ids (no enumeration API; 139 ids at HEAD), get_required_master_paths (no enumeration or dedupe API; 8 paths at HEAD, identical for every locale argument), and build_validation_report (validate_document checks document integrity, not disk existence). Only get_entry is pure delegation to resolve_entry.

SEAL AND BLAST-RADIUS FACTS, MEASURED, THAT BOUND THE TASK 4 COMMIT. scripts/data/DialogicTimelineCatalog.gd is NOT sha256-bound anywhere: all five contract and gate documents were enumerated, 108 bound paths in total, and none is the catalog; neither file Task 4 was originally scoped to modify is bound either. The catalog's NAME appears in sealed prose in evidence/phase_2r/baseline.json and evidence/phase_2r/tooling/codegraph_prerequisites.json, never as a digest, and neither is re-derived from the live tree. Four catalog CONSUMERS are bound in evidence/phase_2r/schedule/gate.json, but those seals read git blobs at subject commit 2bd24eb2ad0c4d76337cf0868257b77a7be666c0 rather than the working tree, and two of the bound files have ALREADY drifted from their recorded digests while the gate still passes, so working-tree edits to consumers cannot invalidate them. The frozen gate runs -gdir=res://tests/unit/tooling WITHOUT -ginclude_subdirs, so a new suite under tests/unit/ does not enter the 25-script count. Zero files under tests/unit/tooling reference the catalog directly; the coupling in Finding 4 is transitive through a preload of GameStateDayResolutionPort.

VERIFICATION DEPTH FOR TASK 4, per the DEVIATION-3 standard and unchanged: new suite RED observed before the production change with zero SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED and zero SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED, then a full mutation campaign reusing the harness at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-2b-campaign with a Task 4 sites file, then GREEN, then BOTH frozen gates unmoved at 25/474/473/1/0/14388 and DOC_VALIDATION PASS packets=16 design_authorities=4 agent_workflow=1, PLUS the four dialogic suites at 4/242/242/11631, PLUS tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd, which Ruling X keeps byte-untouched and which must be proven still green because Task 4 changes the file it preloads. Sibling failure codes must assert a distinguishing MESSAGE fragment and not merely the code, per the 2B lesson. Then ONE fresh read-only reviewer in its own detached worktree of digest-verified pristine bytes, sited outside .godot and .superpowers, then the commit.

DIGEST IMPACT: NONE. No plan bytes and no design bytes change under any of these rulings, so every row of the roadmap Plan Digest Manifest and every implementation_plan_sha256 remain exact.

ALL PRIOR DEVIATIONS STILL BIND. DEVIATION-1 through DEVIATION-7 and Rulings A through T are undisturbed. dwm-oyo.2.1 keeps _is_retired_label and C40; dwm-oyo.2.2 keeps G11, C04, C05 and reviewer findings 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. Neither child bead reserves anything in Task 4's file set, and Task 4 takes nothing from either.

TASK 4's FILE SET AFTER THESE RULINGS, replacing the plan's three: Modify scripts/data/DialogicTimelineCatalog.gd. Create tests/unit/test_dialogic_timeline_catalog.gd plus its .uid. Nothing else. tests/integration/test_profile_reset_consumers.gd is dropped per Ruling Y and tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd is not added per Ruling X.

NEXT ACTION: Phase 01 Task 4 implementation, RED-first, in a fresh session.

comments.text:
TASK 4 IMPLEMENTED AND COMMITTED. RED and GREEN both observed TWICE, once for the authored suite
and again for the suite as amended by the fresh reviewer; a 39-site mutation campaign run twice
against both revisions; ONE fresh read-only reviewer, verdict APPROVE WITH NITS with zero blocking
findings, one important finding FOLDED rather than deferred. Not pushed. DEVIATION-8 and every
ruling it carries were honoured, and one new controller ruling was obtained and is recorded here
in the session that obtained it.

STATE RE-MEASURED AT SESSION OPEN, NOT ASSUMED. Worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-
resealed on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed, HEAD 3c4f28f0b8c5884f337ce32ee4969d8606b9798d, git status
--porcelain -uall EMPTY (0 paths), project.godot
f24d9af7a711db89aaefac4246ddc96e8c6c198a74c69c99aa996a46caf030a6, .godot/phase2r_tests empty.

ALL FOUR BASELINES RE-RUN AT THAT HEAD BEFORE ANY EDIT, AND ALL FOUR EXACT. Frozen tooling gate
25 scripts / 474 tests / 473 passing / 1 documented pending / 0 failing / 14388 asserts, exit 0.
Docs gate DOC_VALIDATION PASS packets=16 design_authorities=4 agent_workflow=1, exit 0, invoked
with the beads snapshot after a bare double dash. Four dialogic suites 4 / 242 / 242 / 11631,
exit 0. tests/unit/test_timeline_manifest.gd 1 / 6 / 6 / 303, exit 0 - measured because Ruling X
keeps that file byte-untouched while Task 4 changes the file it preloads, so it needed a before as
well as an after. Zero [Failed], zero SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED, zero SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED in all of them.

CONTROLLER RULING (e), NEW, AND IT IS THE ONE THING DEVIATION-8 COULD NOT HAVE FORESEEN. The new
suite reaches the five added methods DYNAMICALLY, through tests/support/DynamicScriptProbe.gd and
callv, not by static call syntax. This was not a style choice; it was forced and then measured.
DEVIATION-8 requires a RED with ZERO SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED, but a statically resolved call to a
method the production source does not declare yet is a PARSE error in GDScript, which is exactly a
load failure, so a static-syntax suite can never produce the RED that was ordered. The first
attempt used const CATALOG := preload(...) plus CATALOG.call(&"get_entry", ...) and Godot refused
it: Parse Error: Cannot call non-static function call() on the class DialogicTimelineCatalog
directly. Make an instance instead. MEASURED CAUSE: a preload of a script that declares class_name
resolves to the CLASS, not to a Script object, so Object.call and Object.callv are unavailable on
it. The probe returns a real Script value and the call succeeds. This is the identical idiom
tests/unit/test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd already uses, and it is why that suite could report its
own RED as ordinary assertions. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: writing stub methods
into the catalog first so a static-syntax suite would compile would have made the recorded RED an
observation of already-authored production code, which is weaker evidence and is not what
DEVIATION-8 asked for. The legacy timeline methods are still called by static syntax in the same
suite, because they already exist and their continued existence is itself a Ruling U law.
CARRY-FORWARD: every later task in this plan that adds new methods to an existing class faces
this, so write the new suite against the probe from the start.

WHAT WAS BUILT, EXACTLY THE DEVIATION-8 FILE SET AND NOTHING ELSE.
scripts/data/DialogicTimelineCatalog.gd MODIFIED: 111 insertions, 0 DELETIONS. It is a pure ADD,
which is Ruling U visible in the diff itself; git diff -U0 shows four hunks and every one is
-N,0. The five methods carry the plan's signatures verbatim, including the en literals rather than
the DEFAULT_LOCALE constant, matching the file's own existing get_timeline_path signature.
get_timeline_path gained a four-line deprecation comment and nothing else; it still resolves
through timelines.json. The file header gained a paragraph naming both vocabularies, the 34-id
overlap, the hospital.faint blocker and the forbidden union lookup, so the next reader meets
Ruling U before the code. The entry cache is a SEPARATE pair of static vars from _records, with a
comment saying why one shared table would be the merge Ruling U forbids.
tests/unit/test_dialogic_timeline_catalog.gd CREATED, 21 tests, plus its .uid companion
uid://w5qbf2xt8kq7, generated by a guarded --import and verified unique against every uid token in
the tree.

OBSERVED NUMBERS, BOTH SUITE REVISIONS. Revision A is the authored suite; revision B is revision A
plus the reviewer's finding I-1, and revision B is what is committed.
  A RED, before the production change: 1 script / 20 tests / 1 passing / 19 failing / 14 of 37
    asserts, exit 1, ZERO SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED, ZERO SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED, zero parse errors - so the
    suite genuinely compiled and ran. The single passing test is the one that reads the DELEGATED
    source, DialogicEntryManifest.gd, and finds all four failure codes already declared there.
    That is the same split sub-commit 2A's and 3A's REDs had.
  A GREEN: 1 / 20 / 20 / 0 failing / 552 asserts, exit 0.
  B RED: 1 / 21 / 1 passing / 20 failing / 15 of 39 asserts, exit 1, zero anomalies. RE-OBSERVED
    rather than inferred: the catalog was reverted to its HEAD bytes with git checkout --, the
    suite was run, and the change was restored from a SHA-256-verified snapshot. The committed
    bytes are therefore RED-proven bytes, not bytes that merely resemble them.
  B GREEN: 1 / 21 / 21 / 0 failing / 554 asserts, exit 0.

THE MUTATION CAMPAIGN, RUN TWICE. Harness at C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-task4-campaign, a
sibling of the 2B and Task 3 harnesses, sited outside every worktree so it cannot dirty git
status. It reuses the 2B Run-Campaign.ps1 byte-for-byte apart from three substitutions: campaign
directory, campaign module, default -Gtest. The per-site restore() at the top of the mutate
dispatch is present and commented; that is the line Task 3 lost and contaminated 53 rows with.
A CORRECTION TO THE HANDOFF VOCABULARY WORTH RECORDING: there is no such thing as a sites FILE in
this repository. Sites are declared in a PYTHON MODULE as anchor/replacement pairs and passed to
the driver as a PowerShell string array, exactly as campaign_task3.py does. Each site also carries
its EXPECTED outcome in the module, and analyse_t4.py diffs outcome against expectation, so the
run reports no surprises rather than a bare kill count.
  Against revision A: 39 sites, 33 KILLED, 6 SURVIVED, 0 INVALID, 0 REVIEW, 0 MUTATE_FAILED.
  Against revision B: 39 sites, 34 KILLED, 5 SURVIVED, 0 INVALID, 0 REVIEW, 0 MUTATE_FAILED.
Both runs reported no surprises: every one of the 39 outcomes matched its written expectation.
Every anchor was proven by dryrun to match exactly once before either run, and the tree was proven
byte-exact by SHA-256 against the pristine snapshot after every batch.

THE FIVE REMAINING SURVIVORS, ALL DECLARED BEFORE THE RUN. E02, G01 and R01 are
failure-propagation guards, and V03 is the missing-master branch of build_validation_report;
reaching any of the four needs filesystem manipulation, which is the same category
test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd already records as KNOWINGLY UNCOVERED for its three load-time
codes. E05 is a genuine EQUIVALENT MUTANT: _entries_initialized is a cache flag and clearing it
changes no observable behaviour. E05 also produced a measurement worth keeping - without the flag
the suite took 100 seconds instead of 5, because every get_entry re-ran the published schema over
all 139 records, so the cache controller ruling (d) ordered is a real performance law and not
decoration.

FIVE SITES THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE REST. U01 replaced has_entry_id with the union lookup that
tries the entry vocabulary and falls back to the timeline vocabulary - the exact thing
specification 12.2 forbids and the exact escape hatch DEVIATION-8 warned against - and it DIED to
test_the_entry_and_timeline_vocabularies_stay_separate. P01 changed one character of
get_timeline_path's signature default and died to the preserved-signature pin, so Ruling U's
survival is enforced and not merely asserted. P02 did the same to the ADDED surface, changing
get_entry's default locale from the empty string to en - behaviour-NEUTRAL, because an omitted
locale already becomes en - so only the source-text pin could kill it, and it killed 18 tests
through the _guard cascade. That is also the answer to whether _guard can silently skip a test and
still report green: it cannot, because every guard failure fires a named assertion before
returning. F03 disabled the retired-label branch so a retired id returned the UNKNOWN code
instead, and it died because the test asserts the branch's own MESSAGE fragment AND the ABSENCE of
its sibling's - the 2B lesson, working. D01 deleted the deprecation marker comment and died, so
the plan's mark-it-deprecated bullet is a reachable law rather than prose.

ONE FRESH READ-ONLY REVIEWER, in its own detached worktree at 3c4f28f0b sited outside .godot and
.superpowers, populated from digest-verified pristine bytes, handed the binding rulings so it
could not re-litigate them, and forbidden to run Godot or write anything. VERDICT: APPROVE WITH
NITS, ZERO BLOCKING. It independently re-derived every pinned literal from the shipped JSON - 139,
8, 61, the 34-id intersection, both sorted endpoints, all eight master paths, the hospital locator
path, both disjointness fixture sets and the three retired labels - and every one matched. It
traced the no-guard claim through all seven failure exits of resolve_entry and confirmed no path
exists where a validated document yields a failing resolve. It re-verified Ruling U's own premise
at source: GameStateDayResolutionPort.gd:1089, test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:910, and that
hospital.faint is in timelines.json and absent from dialogic_entries.json. It byte-verified that
all seven legacy timeline methods are identical to HEAD.

ITS ONE IMPORTANT FINDING WAS REAL AND IS FOLDED, NOT DEFERRED. FINDING I-1: the
validate_document CALL inside _ensure_entries is the SOLE guarantor of the unguarded ["value"] and
["entries"] indexes in get_required_master_paths and get_required_entry_ids, and NOTHING pinned
it. Campaign site E03 deleted it and survived, and the declared justification for that survivor -
needs filesystem manipulation - was WRONG. Unlike E02, G01, R01 and V03, E03 is not
filesystem-bound; it is simply invisible to behaviour, because the shipped document is valid. A
future edit could delete the validation, leave the suite green, and leave the two unguarded
indexes one malformed manifest away from an engine error. That is precisely the deletable-in-
silence defect this repository already has a standing rule about. FIXED by pinning the call as
source text in a new test, test_the_cached_entry_document_is_validated_before_it_is_cached, which
is the same idiom the suite already uses three times. E03 now KILLS.

WHY THIS WAS FOLDED WHEN THE 3A REVIEWER FINDINGS WERE NOT. The 3A no-fold, which the maintainer
confirmed on 2026-08-28, rested on two grounds: changing an authored byte would mean the committed
bytes are no longer the campaign-proven bytes, and two of those findings ADDED NEW LAWS, each of
which the DEVIATION-4 carry-forward requires to have its own campaign site, which is a sub-commit
rather than a fold. NEITHER GROUND APPLIES HERE. The site already exists - E03 - so no new site is
created, only its declared expectation flips from survive to kill; and re-proving cost about ten
minutes with a warm harness, so the committed bytes ARE the campaign-proven bytes: RED was
re-observed and the whole 39-site campaign was re-run against revision B. Nothing was taken on
trust. This is a narrower rule than the 3A one, not a contradiction of it: fold a reviewer finding
when an existing campaign site already covers it and re-proving is cheap; defer it when it needs a
site that does not exist yet.

THREE MINOR FINDINGS ALSO FOLDED. M-1: the get_required_master_paths docstring credited
validate_document with refusing a MISSING English locator, but that function's own GDScript
iterates only the locales that exist, so a record with an empty locators object passes all three of
its loops; the refusal actually comes from the published schema validate_document runs, which
requires an en locator with a non-empty path and label. The comment now says so, because it was
sending a future reader to the wrong file. M-2 and M-7: get_required_entry_ids carries the same
unguarded index with no explanation and was the only one of the five added methods with no
docstring at all; it now has one.

THREE MINOR FINDINGS DECLINED, WITH REASONS, SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT RE-RAISE THEM.
M-5, four tests are gated on _guard although they touch only JSON and the delegated manifest: a
correct observation, but the guard is harmless there and removing it would change nothing about
what those tests measure while breaking the uniform opening line every other test has.
M-6, _guard loads the script twice on its null branch: cosmetic, and
tests/unit/test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd's own _guard does exactly the same thing; matching the
sibling suite is worth more than saving one load on a branch that fires only when the catalog is
unloadable.
M-4, build_validation_report reports a clean bill of health for an unloadable manifest - entry
count 0, missing count 0, indistinguishable from success - DECLINED because fixing it makes things
worse by this repository's own standard: an ok or error field would be a new law reachable only by
deleting the shipped manifest, that is, a new permanent survivor. RECORDED AS CARRY-FORWARD
instead. The legacy vocabulary ships validate_all as its loud check and the entry vocabulary has
none, so whoever adds one - most naturally at the Plan 06 cutover - should add it with a fixture
seam rather than as an unreachable guard.
M-3 is an observation rather than an ask and is recorded as such: four mutants, E01, E04, G05 and
R02, kill through an engine error on the unguarded indexes rather than through a returned failure
dictionary. analyse_t4.py classifies all four as KILLED because none is a parse error or a load
failure and each also fails between five and thirteen NAMED tests. That is the deliberate trade
the docstrings make, and the alternative would be exactly the unreachable guard the comments
explain away.

BOTH FROZEN GATES AND EVERY NAMED SUITE RE-RUN AT THE FINAL COMMITTED TREE, ALL UNMOVED.
Frozen tooling gate 25 scripts / 474 tests / 473 passing / 1 documented pending / 0 failing /
14388 asserts, exit 0. Docs gate DOC_VALIDATION PASS packets=16 design_authorities=4
agent_workflow=1, exit 0. Four dialogic suites 4 / 242 / 242 / 11631, exit 0. tests/unit/
test_timeline_manifest.gd 1 / 6 / 6 / 303, exit 0, byte-untouched as Ruling X orders and green
against the changed file it preloads. New suite 1 / 21 / 21 / 554, exit 0. Zero [Failed], zero
SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED, zero SCRIPT_LOAD_FAILED and zero parse errors in all five. HEAD, the boundary

THE FROZEN GATE CAN STILL END UNMOVED at 25/474/473/1/0/14388, but ONLY if the commit carries a regenerated desktop_contract.json (tools/evidence/generate_desktop_contract.gd; reseal precedent 59d14b027) IN THE SAME COMMIT as the bridge edit, so no committed tree ever fails the gate. minesweeper_contract.json intersects Task 5 only at project.godot; the amendment contracts bind nothing Task 5 touches; evidence/phase_2r/schedule/gate.json's file digest for the bridge reads git blobs at 2bd24eb2 and TOLERATES working-tree drift (Task 4 pre-flight already proved two bound files drifted green) - but its declared_surface list is enforced LIVE by test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:548-569 via get_file_as_string, so every declared bridge symbol must STAY PRESENT with its exact spelling (func start_timeline_path(path,context), func start_timeline_id(timeline_id,context), func capture_restore_state(), func _on_runtime_timeline_ended(), signal timeline_finished(timeline_id: String, result: Dictionary)) and func finish_current_timeline must STAY ABSENT. LEGACY RESULT SHAPE IS PRE-HOUSE. start_timeline_id/start_timeline_path fail with ok false plus a reason String key - no code key, six sites at bridge :159-:196 - and :169-:172 already implements an English-path fallback. 9. HOUSE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS FOR THE HARD PARTS. Receipts: SaveManagerNarrativeCheckpointPort.gd:80-89 and :118-121 - canonical JSON + sha256_text fingerprint, duplicate-identical returns ok true + value.duplicate true + THE STORED RECEIPT, conflict returns duplicate_transaction_conflict and mutates nothing. Envelope precedent: _start_playback returns code started with semantic fields in RECEIPT and value {}. Port configure template: configure_narrative_checkpoint_port :370-380. DEVIATION-11 (Phase 01 Task 6 pre-flight: eleven measured plan defects and the four rulings that dispose of them). MAINTAINER-RATIFIED 2026-08-31 via AskUserQuestion, recorded in the session that obtained the rulings. NO CODE was written, NO suite was run, NO byte changed.

STATE RE-MEASURED AT SESSION OPEN, NOT ASSUMED. Worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-resealed on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed, HEAD 2673550e47271fa9a638a7b821effc6a9096b9b7, git status --porcelain -uall EMPTY (0 paths), project.godot f24d9af7a711db89aaefac4246ddc96e8c6c198a74c69c99aa996a46caf030a6 (unmoved, and pinned in exactly two files: evidence/phase_2r/handoff/desktop_contract.json and .../minesweeper_contract.json). BASELINES WERE DELIBERATELY NOT RE-RUN. This session ran no Godot at all, so the nine baselines recorded at Task 5 close stand as the last measured values and the implementation session MUST re-run them at its own open before any edit. Zero leaked sandboxes; .godot/phase2r_tests untouched.

METHOD. Nine parallel read-only measurement agents, one per Task 6 premise dimension, then adversarial verifiers that re-derived each finding at source independently. 87 raw findings; 15 reached verification before an API session limit stopped the remaining 14 verifiers and the completeness critic; 11 CONFIRMED, 4 REFUTED. Every finding below was additionally re-confirmed by the controller at source. Confidence is stated honestly per finding; four dimensions (DtlStructureValidator, ArtManifest tail) carry controller confirmation but not independent adversarial confirmation, and that is marked.

FINDING 1, BULLET 1's SECOND RED IS ALREADY DELIVERED. "DTL cannot compose a resource path" is tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd:82 DTL_DYNAMIC_RESOURCE_PATH, emitted at :245 whenever a line contains res://, user:// or load(. It is already asserted by tests/unit/test_dtl_master_structure.gd, including against res://art/portraits/lavinia.png at :652 and :770 - an asset that has never existed. Shipped by Task 3.

FINDING 2, BULLET 4's PAYLOAD HALF IS ALREADY DELIVERED, IN A DIFFERENT FILE. scripts/narrative/DialogicEntryManifest.gd:694 validate_signal enforces the exact registered payload field set (SIGNAL_PAYLOAD_FIELD_MISSING :718, SIGNAL_PAYLOAD_FIELD_UNKNOWN :722, SIGNAL_OPAQUE_FIELD_INVALID :730) plus entry grant, stage legality, echo binding and reply ownership, and delegates line_id/witnessed_line_id to validate_line_id (:736) and presentation_atom_id to validate_atom_id (:740). DialogicBridge.gd:763 calls it. DTL carries no JSON at all, so DtlStructureValidator has no surface for this law.

FINDING 3, BULLET 4's VISUAL HALF IS ALREADY REFUSED, MORE STRONGLY. Measured across all 69 .dtl files (8 masters plus 61 legacy): ZERO occurrences of background, character, portrait or res://. DtlStructureValidator is a CLOSED whitelist - _classify (:239) is reached only for lines the whitelist already rejected, and the terminal fallback is DTL_DIALOGUE_LINE (:257). Naming Background/Character/Portrait would be a WEAKER, more specific law layered on a stronger general one, and admitting registered visual events would mean RELAXING the whitelist, which the file's own KNOWN LIMITS block forbids: it says a future authored mode must RE-SCOPE the validator rather than relax it in place. Controller-confirmed; the adversarial verifiers for this dimension did not run.

FINDING 4, BULLET 3's STRUCTURAL-MODE CLAUSE IS ALREADY DELIVERED AND ALREADY FROZEN. All 139 records in data/manifests/dialogic_entries.json carry visual_ids {required: [], optional: []} - measured 0 non-empty. schemas/manifests/dialogic-entries.schema.json closes that object with additionalProperties false and required [optional, required]. tests/unit/test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd:798 test_visual_ids_are_empty_in_structural_mode already pins it, and its own assertion messages cite plan Task 6 by name. Inside the frozen four-suite baseline.

FINDING 5, BULLET 3's NEUTRAL FALLBACK CANNOT BE POPULATED. The repository owns exactly ONE non-addon image: icon.svg (git ls-files filtered on png/jpg/jpeg/webp/svg, minus addons/, count 1; 173 including addons). No verified neutral background, character or portrait asset exists. By bullet 3's own rule - "the neutral fallback record is added only when an existing verified neutral asset exists" - the registry ships EMPTY. NOTE THE VERIFIER'S CORRECTION, which the controller accepted: this does NOT make the RED tests unwritable. The refusal direction is writable with no asset at all, and HEAD already does exactly that six times (see Finding 1). Only the AFFIRMATIVE resolution path stays unexercised. scripts/data/DataCatalog.gd separately composes res://art/ on six lines (111, 112, 113, 195, 301, 325), so ArtManifest would not be the single art authority even after the rewrite.

FINDING 6, ArtManifest IS A GENUINE STUB WITH ZERO CALLERS. scripts/data/ArtManifest.gd is 11 lines, six statics all returning empty. git grep ArtManifest over '*.gd' returns exactly ONE line - its own class_name at :1. No production caller, no test. The rewrite is therefore free of breakage, but it also creates a registry with no consumer, which is the same "new law with no consumer" pattern on which Task 5 declined findings M-2 and M-3.

FINDING 7, THE DECISIVE BLOCKER: BULLET 2 REDDENS THREE SUITES, ONE OF THEM FROZEN, IN ANY IMPLEMENTATION. data/manifests/dialogic_ids.json registers exactly 18 reply_lines, all of shape line.contact.ordinary.{lavinia,sylvia,priscilla}.day{1..6}.reply.{a,b,c}, covering 6 of 139 entries - while all 139 grant history.line.witness. Every line id that live suites feed to mark_line_visited is UNREGISTERED, measured against both candidate laws (reply_lines membership AND line_namespace ownership across all 139 namespaces): "opening.day1.line.1" and "opening.day1.line.9" and "dating.solo.sylvia.day3.line.1" (tests/unit/test_profile_manager.gd:219, :222, :229, :244), "line.reset-proof" (tests/integration/test_profile_reset_consumers.gd:81, the FROZEN profile reset 3/3/102 baseline), "settings-reset-line" (tests/scene/test_settings_localization_scene.gd:80). The namespace escape hatch is FORECLOSED by DEVIATION-4 Ruling E, recorded in DialogicEntryManifest.gd itself: a stranger that happens to sit under the owner's line_namespace is still refused, because membership there is registration.

FINDING 8, A SCOPE CLAIM THE PRE-FLIGHT RAISED AND THEN REFUTED ITSELF. Four measurement agents concluded bullet 2 was not implementable inside Task 6's file set, because validate_line_id (:652) requires an entry_id that mark_line_visited(line_id) (:161) does not have. The adversarial verifier REFUTED that and the controller confirmed the refutation: load_ids_default() (:479) is PUBLIC and returns the whole ids document, reply_lines is a top-level public key, and its 18 records are globally unique and self-describe owning_entry_id - so an entry_id-free existence check is implementable entirely inside autoload/ProfileManager.gd, with no new manifest function, no arity change, no edit to the sha256-bound DialogicBridge.gd and no re-seal. The verifier also refuted the secondary fear that adding a public static moves the four-suite baseline: both method-surface assertions (test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd:1388-1395 and test_dialogic_ids_manifest.gd:1490-1494) are presence-only over a fixed const list, not exact-set matches.

FINDING 9, THE VISITED-LINE SUBSYSTEM HAS NO PRODUCTION WRITER AND ITS ONE ENTRANCE IS BROKEN. mark_line_visited has ZERO reachable production writers at HEAD. configure_skip_context has no production caller (definition at DialogicBridge.gd:440 plus three sites in tests/integration/test_dialogic_skip.gd only). configure_narrative_bridge has NO caller anywhere - defined at scripts/ui/DialogueBox.gd:27, delegated at scripts/ui/DatingScene.gd:77-80, and nothing in autoload/, scripts/application/ or tests/ calls it. And DialogicBridge.request_skip_step (:456) reads its line id from _runtime_adapter.current_line_id() (:459) - a method defined ONLY on the _FakeAdapter at tests/integration/test_dialogic_skip.gd:44 and ABSENT from the production scripts/narrative/DialogicRuntimeAdapter.gd. So the path short-circuits at :457-458 with skip_context_not_configured today, and would be a hard runtime error the moment anyone wires it. Separately, classify_next_event() returns &"unknown" unconditionally (DialogicRuntimeAdapter.gd:134-137). This is the entrance bullet 2 actually exists to guard, and specification 12.6 forbids exactly this class of identity: IDs are not derived from file path, line number, translated text, or label position.

FINDING 10, A MISSING PREDECESSOR DELIVERABLE NOBODY HAD RECORDED. DEVIATION-3 ordered a visuals registry as sub-commit 2C. IT WAS NEVER BUILT. The plan's own Task Interface Map row 6 (plan line 35) says Task 6 CONSUMES "ID/atom/visual registries". The ID and atom halves exist; the visual half does not. The visual record shape has THREE competing homes in the authority set: the entry record (specification 12.2), a data manifest (DEVIATION-3), and a GDScript class (the plan's Task 6 block). Related: the plan makes "required" a property of the visual record, while the specification and HEAD make it a property of the (entry, visual) edge via visual_ids.required. Also measured: "structural mode" is a PLAN-ONLY term; the specification never uses it.

FINDING 11, SCOPE COLLISION WITH dwm-oyo.2.2, AND DEVIATION-8's NO-FOLD GROUND DISSOLVES. dwm-oyo.2.2 Part B Findings 1, 2 and 6 all live in tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd - the exact file Task 6 bullet 4 modifies. DEVIATION-8 Item Zero justified deferring them partly because "Task 4 touches none of the affected files"; Task 6 does. Its owner suite tests/unit/test_dtl_master_structure.gd is one of the four frozen dialogic suites, so ANY new validator law moves 4/242/242/11631. Housekeeping: dwm-oyo.2.2's acceptance criteria still cite 14388 asserts; the true frozen figure has been 14394 since Task 5.

CORRECTION THE CONTROLLER OWES, MADE HERE RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING. Mid-session the controller reported that Task 6 could not touch ProfileManager.gd or ArtManifest.gd without a same-commit re-seal, because evidence/phase_2r/runtime/game_state_surface.json records call sites as exact file:line (autoload/ProfileManager.gd:30, :243, :246, :255, :264 and scripts/data/ArtManifest.gd:9) and its sha256 is cross-bound at tests/unit/tooling/test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:1219, inside the frozen 25. THAT WAS AN OVERCORRECTION. The binding is file-to-RECORD, not file-to-SOURCE: :1219 compares the committed surface's bytes against a digest stored in the committed record; tests/unit/test_game_state_facade_contract.gd:60-72 reads only the day record's disposition; and tests/unit/tooling/test_public_surface_inventory.gd:242 regenerates into a SCRATCH path and checks canonicality only. Nothing re-derives those line numbers from live source. Editing either file therefore reddens NO gate - it silently staleness the recorded lines. Ruling D below disposes of the residual debt.

RULING A (LINE LAW HOME). Task 6 delivers the visited-line identity law as a CONFIGURED SEAM on autoload/ProfileManager.gd - a configure_line_registry-shaped entry point that makes mark_line_visited strict ONLY when a registry is configured, and leaves it permissive when it is not. RATIONALE: it is implementable entirely inside Task 6's named file set (Finding 8), it keeps all five legacy literals passing so NO frozen baseline moves (Finding 7), and it matches this repository's own established precedent for exactly this problem - configure_mutation_gate (ProfileManager.gd:30), configure_skip_context (DialogicBridge.gd:440) and Task 5's configure_signal_command_port / configure_playback_completion_port. RED and GREEN are driven through the configured seam, so the law is fixture-reachable and individually mutation-killable, which DEVIATION-4 controller ruling 1 requires. REJECTED: an unconditional check in ProfileManager, which would force amending three suites including a frozen baseline in the same commit; and validating at the skip entrance in DialogicBridge, which is sha256-bound in the handoff desktop_contract and whose every new public method is +1 against the frozen 14394 assert figure.

RULING B (VALIDATOR RING-FENCE). Task 6 does NOT touch tools/dialogic/DtlStructureValidator.gd. Bullet 4 is already delivered, and more strongly, by the closed whitelist plus DTL_DYNAMIC_RESOURCE_PATH (Findings 1, 2, 3), and the file's own KNOWN LIMITS block says a future authored mode must re-scope it rather than relax it in place. The 76-site Task 3 campaign proved those exact bytes; leaving them byte-identical keeps that proof valid, holds the frozen four-suite 4/242/242/11631, and keeps dwm-oyo.2.2 whole as a single batched campaign. REJECTED: folding dwm-oyo.2.2 Findings 1, 2 and 6 into Task 6 - the fold is legitimate now that the no-fold ground has dissolved, but it buys real gaps at the cost of a moved frozen baseline and new campaign sites, and it belongs to the bead that already owns it.

RULING C (VISUALS). Task 6 ships CLOSURE LAWS ONLY, over an EMPTY typed registry inside scripts/data/ArtManifest.gd. The strict record shape {visual_id, resource_path, resource_type, required, fallback_visual_id} and its refusal laws - required missing or wrong-type rejects; an optional visual resolves only to a DECLARED neutral fallback id - are authored and proven in the REFUSAL direction against fabricated fixtures, which the repo already does six times for nonexistent art paths (Findings 1, 5). NO art path is invented and NO neutral fallback record is created, because no verified neutral asset exists (Finding 5). NO new data manifest and NO new schema file are created for a registry with zero records. REJECTED: building the missing sub-commit 2C registry the 1c4682a33 way (manifest + schema + parser + suite + uid), which ships five artifacts the plan names none of, all empty; and deferring visuals wholesale, which would leave the Phase 01 Verification Gate line "context, signals, lines, atoms, and visuals are closed" unmet. CARRY-FORWARD: the affirmative resolution path stays KNOWINGLY UNEXERCISED until a real asset exists, exactly as observer.evidence.commit denial is knowingly uncovered; and the "required" home conflict (plan = property of the visual, specification 12.2 and HEAD = property of the entry/visual edge) is resolved in favour of the SPECIFICATION, since visual_ids.required already ships on all 139 entries.

RULING D (SURFACE FRESHNESS). Task 6 regenerates evidence/phase_2r/runtime/game_state_surface.json and re-seals its schedule-gate record in the SAME commit, using the standard amendment re-seal recipe: frozen subject on the code commit, delete-then-regenerate the contracts, never rewrite a historical gate. It is a co-generated sibling artifact, so regenerating both together keeps the digests internally consistent. This is elective rather than forced (see the CORRECTION above), and it is chosen so the committed evidence keeps pointing at the right lines instead of rotting silently.

WHAT TASK 6 ACTUALLY DELIVERS AFTER THESE RULINGS. A configured line-identity seam on ProfileManager with RED-first proof through the seam; an empty but strictly typed visual registry in ArtManifest with its refusal laws proven against fabricated fixtures; the two new suites at tests/unit/test_dialogic_identity_registries.gd and tests/unit/test_art_manifest.gd (plus the two .gd.uid companions the plan does not name - the repo is at full uid coverage and commit 43df2d43f exists solely to repair missing ones); and a regenerated surface with its re-sealed record. DtlStructureValidator.gd is NOT touched. The frozen 25 stays 25 because the new suites go to tests/unit/, not tests/unit/tooling/, which is a directory glob.

CARRY-FORWARD FOR THE IMPLEMENTER. (1) Re-run all nine baselines at session open BEFORE any edit; this session ran none. (2) Ruling A's seam means the RED must be driven through the configured registry - a first-run green proves nothing, so mutate, observe, revert byte-identically, and report OBSERVED numbers. (3) Neither load_default nor load_ids_default caches; a per-call FileAccess read plus StrictJson parse of 11,154 bytes (ids) or 85,428 bytes (entries) is the cost of a naive implementation, and the seam design must settle this BEFORE RED is written because the RED shape depends on it. (4) dwm-oyo.2.1 reserves the injected-registry seam for _is_retired_label; Ruling A builds a sibling of exactly that shape, so check whether the same seam closes C40 and, if it does, add the campaign site and close 2.1. (5) dwm-oyo.2.2 stays OPEN and OUT of scope under Ruling B, and its acceptance criteria need 14388 corrected to 14394 when next touched. (6) Finding 9's broken skip path is NOT repaired by Task 6 as scoped; it is a live production defect - request_skip_step calls a method the production adapter does not define - and it needs its own bead. (7) Fourteen adversarial verifiers and the completeness critic did not run (API session limit), so Findings 3, 5 and 6 carry controller confirmation only; re-derive them at source before relying on them.

NEXT ACTION: Phase 01 Task 6 implementation in a fresh session under Rulings A-D, RED-first, baselines re-measured at session open.

DEVIATION-12 (Phase 01 Task 6 implementation session open: nine baselines re-measured, the three unverified pre-flight findings re-derived and partly corrected, one new blocking discovery that falsifies Ruling D's premise, and three rulings that dispose of it). MAINTAINER-RATIFIED 2026-09-01 via AskUserQuestion, recorded in the session that obtained the rulings. NO production byte changed; the tree is clean at 0 paths.

STATE RE-MEASURED AT SESSION OPEN, NOT ASSUMED. Worktree C:/Users/glori/Documents/dwm-p2r13-resealed on codex/dwm-p2r13-resealed, HEAD 2673550e47271fa9a638a7b821effc6a9096b9b7, git status --porcelain -uall EMPTY (0 paths), project.godot f24d9af7a711db89aaefac4246ddc96e8c6c198a74c69c99aa996a46caf030a6 unmoved, .godot/phase2r_tests EMPTY (zero leaked sandboxes) before and after every run.

ALL NINE BASELINES RE-RUN BEFORE ANY EDIT, AND ALL NINE EXACT, as DEVIATION-11 carry-forward item 1 required. OBSERVED: tooling gate 25 scripts / 474 tests / 473 passing / 1 documented pending / 0 failing / 14394 asserts, with 25/25 scripts confirmed executed and zero SUITE_NOT_EXECUTED; docs gate DOC_VALIDATION PASS packets=16 design_authorities=4 agent_workflow=1; four dialogic unit suites 4/242/242/11631; timeline manifest 1/6/6/303; catalog 1/21/21/554; bridge contract 1/14/14/275; profile reset 1/3/3/102; runtime adapter 1/9/9/22; six-suite dialogic family 6/59/59/520. Every one of the nine SUITE COMPOSITIONS was recovered mechanically from the executed-path lines of the Task 5 task5-base-*.log files rather than reconstructed from prose, so these are the same sets and not lookalikes. Godot was run strictly serialized, one process at a time, with a ten-minute timeout on the four-minute tooling gate. HEAD, project.godot and the sandbox directory were re-verified after the batch.

FINDING 3 RE-DERIVED AT SOURCE AND PARTLY CORRECTED. The repository holds 70 .dtl files, not 69: the 70th is tests/fixtures/dialogic/phase2r_contract_fixture.dtl, outside the dialogic/ tree the pre-flight enumerated. The zero-occurrence claim HOLDS and is now proven rather than asserted: background, character, portrait, res://, user:// and load( occur zero times across all 70 files, case-sensitive and case-insensitive, by three independent methods, with POSITIVE CONTROLS establishing the greps actually reached every file (git grep -o -F -- : returns 1016 matches; git grep -I -l returns all 70, so none is skipped as binary). Two corrections to the pre-flight's reasoning. First, CLOSED WHITELIST is closed over LINE SHAPES, not over LINE CONTENT: three of the seven accept branches are begins_with prefix matches (:129 label , :155 # PURPOSE: , :159 # ALLOWED SIGNALS: ), so a line reading label res://art/portraits/lavinia.png contains res:// yet is swallowed before _classify and degrades to DTL_UNREGISTERED_LABEL, a different code with a different message; and a # PURPOSE: res:// line outside any open label block produces no failure of any code at all. All six hazard-injection tests mutate the one exact-equality branch, so this escape is entirely untested. Second, the owner suite refuses exactly ONE distinct fabricated art path, not six. Unchanged and confirmed: DTL_DYNAMIC_RESOURCE_PATH declared at :82, emitted at :244-246, trigger set exactly the three substrings res:// | user:// | load( with no fourth token; the KNOWN LIMITS block at :50-54 requires a future authored mode to RE-SCOPE rather than relax in place; and the validator carries ZERO executable surface naming Background, Character or Portrait, the only mention being a doc comment at :8.

FINDING 5 RE-DERIVED AT SOURCE AND UPHELD. The repository owns exactly ONE non-addon image file, icon.svg, out of 173 tracked png/jpg/jpeg/webp/svg. Widening the extension set does not change the answer; the .import sidecars corroborate; no untracked image hides on disk; no .tres or .tscn wraps a texture; and an art/ directory does not exist at all, nor assets/ nor res/. scripts/data/DataCatalog.gd composes res://art/ on exactly the six cited lines 111, 112, 113, 195, 301, 325, and every one of those six composed paths points at a file that does NOT exist. Two corrections. The pre-flight's six existing refusals over nonexistent art paths is really TWO refusal assertions citing a res://art path; the six it was remembering are the six visual-identity constraint assertions in test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd, which likewise need no asset. And two tracked background images DO exist inside the vendored addon at addons/dialogic/Example Assets/backgrounds/; they are vendor demo content, not game content, and the registry still ships EMPTY on that basis. The conclusion is unchanged: no verified neutral asset exists, the refusal direction is writable with no asset at all, and the affirmative resolution path stays knowingly unexercised.

FINDING 6 RE-DERIVED AT SOURCE AND UPHELD WITH ONE CORRECTION. scripts/data/ArtManifest.gd is 11 lines with six statics all returning empty, and it has ZERO callers - confirmed after widening the search from the pre-flight's *.gd pathspec to the entire tracked tree AND the entire working tree, including .tscn, .tres, .cfg, project.godot and the global script class cache. THE CORRECTION: it DOES have a tracked .gd.uid companion, so the repo-wide scripts/ pairing invariant is intact and Task 6 must ship .uid companions for any new .gd. Also corrected: game_state_surface.json recording scripts/data/ArtManifest.gd:9 is literally true but semantically misleading - it is a scanner false positive on the parameter name in get_daily_main_scene_paths(day: int), recorded as a call site of the GameState day property, not a record about ArtManifest. ArtManifest.gd is not itself sha256-sealed anywhere.

FROZEN-GATE IMMUNITY ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED, because Ruling A adds a public method to an autoload and the tooling gate's assert figure is data-driven. autoload/ProfileManager.gd and scripts/data/ArtManifest.gd appear in NEITHER REQUIRED_SURFACE_ENTRIES nor ABSENT_SURFACE_SYMBOLS in tools/evidence/generate_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd, and in fact appear NOWHERE in that generator or in tests/unit/tooling/test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd; git grep ProfileManager over tools/ returns nothing. The per-declared-public-entry walk at test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:557-563 - the mechanism that moved 14388 to 14394 when Task 5 added six public bridge methods - therefore cannot reach Task 6's files. test_public_surface_inventory.gd's record-count assertions run against a synthetic seven-symbol fixture, and its live rebuild checks signatures and dispositions, not call sites. test_no_unconditional_pass.gd's repository walk asserts ONCE over the whole of res://tests, not once per file, so two new suites add zero asserts - but it does bind Task 6 to never write a test whose only effective assertion is assert_true(true) or pass_test(). DECLARED EXPECTATION: Rulings A and C move no frozen count. This is a prediction to be checked against the observed post-edit gate, not a settled fact.

dwm-oyo.2.1 AND CAMPAIGN SITE C40 ARE NOT CLOSED BY THIS DESIGN, answering DEVIATION-11 carry-forward item 4 in the negative. Ruling A's seam is a SIBLING of the _is_retired_label injected-registry seam, not the same mechanism: different file (autoload/ProfileManager.gd versus scripts/narrative/DialogicEntryManifest.gd:825-832), different injection style (a configured setter on an autoload versus a per-call parameter on a static func), different block of the same registry (reply_lines versus retired_ids), and no shared call path, since _is_retired_label's only caller is resolve_entry:358. C40 rewrites :831 to return true and SURVIVED in both recorded campaign waves because load_ids_default() reads from disk without validating, leaving the false branch unreachable. Closing it would edit DialogicEntryManifest.gd and move the frozen four-suite baseline. Do not claim it. Related housekeeping, corrected: dwm-oyo.2.2's stale 14388 figure is in its DESCRIPTION, not its acceptance criteria, which inherit it by reference.

THE NEW DISCOVERY THAT FALSIFIES RULING D'S PREMISE, measured rather than reasoned. I regenerated evidence/phase_2r/runtime/game_state_surface.json at a CLEAN HEAD with zero Task 6 edits, through the isolated runner, using tools/runtime/generate_public_surface_inventory.gd. IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE: committed d09fb54614ac6861f7a98ebff6719e4b0c9ae540ede5d309693f3267b9c1e089 became 70f9346df83213d42ef57d4a52f6ad3b4b12aa7e93c9cdf7cf8a684e4cfb2ee8. Forty-eight of 208 records differ plus one entirely new dynamic_reference key (request_schedule_done). The drift is large and old: ApplicationBootstrap call sites move by hundreds of lines (302 to 398, 672 to 834, 760 to 1261), SaveManager 380 to 492 and 949 to 1085, and whole files that did not exist when the surface was generated now appear (GameStateDesktopConditionContextPort.gd, GameStateMinesweeperShopPort.gd). THE COMMITTED SURFACE IS ALREADY MASSIVELY STALE AT HEAD, AND TASK 6 DID NOT CAUSE ANY OF IT. Note also that the generator hard-pins --output to its TARGETS table, so this could not be probed into a scratch path; the file was regenerated in place and then restored with git checkout, and the tree was re-verified at 0 paths with the digest back to d09fb546 before anything else ran. Equally important, the re-seal is NOT forced, contrary to a mid-session reading: test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:1218-1219 compares the committed FILE's bytes against the digest stored in the committed RECORD (gate.json member generated_surface), so both stay put and the gate stays GREEN if the surface is never regenerated. DEVIATION-11 was right to call Ruling D elective; it was wrong only in believing Task 6 would be what made the file stale.

RULING 12-A (SURFACE FRESHNESS, SUPERSEDING DEVIATION-11 RULING D). Task 6 leaves evidence/phase_2r/runtime/game_state_surface.json BYTE-UNTOUCHED and performs no schedule-gate re-seal. RATIONALE: the rot is pre-existing, forty-eight records wide, and traces to no part of Task 6; folding it into this commit would put a large unrelated diff inside an exact-path boundary whose whole purpose is that every changed line traces to the request. The gate stays green either way, verified empirically. The drift gets its OWN bead. REJECTED: executing Ruling D as written, which buys freshness at the cost of an unattributable commit; and paying the drift in a separate prior commit, which is honest but costs two extra commits and two gate.json regenerations, and gate.json regeneration additionally re-hashes working-tree logs and can fail command_log_missing, a risk not yet probed and not worth taking inside Task 6.

RULING 12-B (NO PRODUCTION WIRING). configure_line_registry lands TEST-ONLY. It is not called from autoload/ApplicationBootstrap.gd or anywhere else in production. RATIONALE: this matches Task 5's precedent, which landed two of its three ports test-only, and only configure_narrative_checkpoint_port among the five precedent seams has a production caller at all. Wiring would edit ApplicationBootstrap.gd, which is sha256-bound in BOTH handoff contracts source_bindings, forcing a handoff re-seal no ruling orders; and it would flip all five measured legacy line literals from green to red in the same stroke, including tests/integration/test_profile_reset_consumers.gd:81 line.reset-proof inside the FROZEN 3/3/102 baseline. The permissive-when-unconfigured default is exactly what protects them.

RULING 12-C (PLAN BULLET 4 CLOSES BY RECORD). The fourth Task 6 bullet - extend static validation to reject raw unregistered Background/Character/Portrait paths and unsafe JSON signal payloads - is closed BY RECORD, with no code. The DTL half is barred by Ruling B and is moot in practice (zero occurrences across all 70 .dtl files, proven with positive controls) and already refused by DTL_DYNAMIC_RESOURCE_PATH for every line that reaches _classify. The payload half already ships in DialogicEntryManifest.validate_signal:694, which enforces the exact registered payload field set and delegates every embedded id to its owning validator; extending it would edit DialogicEntryManifest.gd and move the frozen 4/242/242/11631 baseline.

THE SETTLED DESIGN, to be implemented RED-first. THE COST OF TOUCHING autoload/DialogicBridge.gd, MEASURED THREE WAYS AND ADVERSARIALLY VERIFIED.

FIRST, the plus-one-per-public-entry rule is EXACT and was proven by a historical control rather than by reading. tools/evidence/generate_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:458-513 parse_declared_surface collects, at COLUMN ZERO only, lines beginning signal / static func / func, and drops any name beginning with underscore except _init; const, var, enum, class_name and indented or inner-class declarations are invisible to it. tests/unit/tooling/test_phase2r_schedule_gate.gd:560-563 iterates EVERY collected entry and asserts once per entry, reading the WORKING TREE through FileAccess, not a git blob. NINE MEASURED TASK 7 PLAN DEFECTS.

DEFECT 1. tests/integration/test_dialogic_restore.gd ALREADY EXISTS. The plan block says Create. It is 9681 bytes, 207 lines, 11 tests, 24 static asserts, and its own header attributes it to dwm-p2r.8 Plan-05 Task 2 Step 2.4 - an EARLIER plan. It is a member of the FROZEN six-suite family, contributing 11 of the 59 tests and 24 of the 520 asserts. The correct verb is Modify, and every test added to it moves that frozen figure.

DEFECT 2. THE BRIDGE HALF OF TASK 7 WAS ALREADY SHIPPED BY TASK 5. The plan's own Task 5 block specifies resume_entry by signature and says restore revalidates the durable semantic checkpoint and issues a fresh token. autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:628 resume_entry already exact-key-validates the checkpoint, cross-checks stage against frozen_context expected_stage and transaction_id against frozen_context transaction_id, refuses an undeclared execution mode, resolves through the catalog get_entry, refuses a missing master with entry_master_missing, revalidates content_version with entry_content_version_mismatch, fingerprints the frozen context with sha256_text, mints a fresh monotonic process-local resume token, and retains transaction_id in _active_entry. DEFECT 3. resume_entry HAS ZERO PRODUCTION CALLERS. A repo-wide grep returns thirteen hits: the declaration plus twelve inside tests/integration/test_dialogic_signal_boundary.gd. Task 7's real content is making the restore participant its FIRST caller.

DEFECT 4. THE SIX-FIELD PREPARED PLAN CANNOT BE PASSED TO resume_entry. autoload/DialogicBridge.gd:33 _RESUME_CHECKPOINT_KEYS is exactly five - content_version, entry_id, frozen_context, stage, transaction_id - and is enforced by _exact_keys at :634. DEFECT 6. SECTION 10.1 IS A MIS-CITATION. Task 7 cites Sections 10.1, 12.4, 14.3-14.4. Section 10.1 Active-board snapshot is entirely about the minesweeper board instance; zero of its eight enumerated fields appear in Task 7's six-field plan shape, its operative rule that loading an active board never regenerates it has no plan bullet, and board restore is measurably owned by scripts/application/restore/DesktopBoardRestoreParticipant.gd under Plan 02 Task 6.

DEFECT 7. THE PARTICIPANT IS ALREADY PRODUCTION-WIRED. autoload/ApplicationBootstrap.gd:39 preloads NarrativeRestoreParticipant.gd, so upgrading the participant changes production behaviour even with ApplicationBootstrap byte-identical. ApplicationBootstrap.gd is bound in BOTH handoff contracts, so it must stay byte-identical or minesweeper_contract.json joins the boundary.

DEFECT 8. THE CURRENT PREPARED PLAN CARRIES A PHYSICAL PATH. NarrativeRestoreParticipant.gd:51-57 puts timeline_path and timeline_id into the plan, which specification 12.4 and 14.4 forbid persisting. The Task 7 six-field shape removes it, but no plan bullet names that removal as a law. Separately, resume_entry's success receipt returns path and label to its caller at DialogicBridge.gd:712-720, so finalize will receive physical locators it must neither store nor return.

DEFECT 9. SPEC OBLIGATIONS CITED BUT UNCOVERED. Specification 14.4 lists eleven persisted items against the plan's six declared as only; requires an explicit migration map and contract-version bump for a breaking semantic change, which Task 7 introduces and does not provide; names four rejection classes (future, malformed, corrupt, unmappable) where the plan names two; requires rejection without overwriting the slot or partially mutating run or profile state, which no RED item tests; forbids substituting another route, which the plan drops while importing two rules of different scope from 14.1 and 12.4; and defines a five-step cross-store transaction journal whose step four is an explicit load-time duty, entirely absent from Task 7. Specification 14.3 forks on before-receipt restart versus after-receipt continuation, which the plan collapses into a single resume_entry call. Specification 12.3's frozen-context field law is unrepresented - the plan types frozen_context as a bare Dictionary.

RULING 14-A (WHERE prepare VALIDATES). Task 7 adds EXACTLY ONE new column-zero public method to autoload/DialogicBridge.gd, a PURE validator that resolves and revalidates a resume checkpoint WITHOUT starting Dialogic, and prepare calls it. DECLARED COST, to be checked against the observed post-edit gate rather than assumed: the tooling assert figure moves 14394 to 14395 and NOTHING ELSE moves. RATIONALE: specification 12.4's chain makes the bridge the sole narrative seam, and the alternative - the participant resolving through the injected catalog itself - creates a second, weaker copy of the resolution law whose acceptance set can DIVERGE from finalize's. That divergence is precisely the failure the task exists to prevent: a restore that passes prepare, commits the checkpoint journal, and then fails inside finalize after the transaction is already past its rollback point. One assert is the correct price for making prepare and finalize share one refusal vocabulary. REJECTED: participant-side validation (0 asserts, divergence risk); bridge-private-helpers-only (0 asserts, but leaves prepare with no non-starting validator and so forces it around the bridge anyway).

RULING 15-A (manifest_fingerprint REUSES THE SHIPPED PRODUCER, SUPERSEDING DEVIATION-14 IMPLEMENTER DECISION 2). MAINTAINER-RATIFIED 2026-09-01 via AskUserQuestion at Task 7 session open, recorded in the session that obtained it, BEFORE any byte was edited. Tree clean at 0 paths, HEAD ae5d91898edb984c1ba5fdffa7caa9dede391bf1.

WHAT DEVIATION-14 DECIDED. Implementer decision 2 defined manifest_fingerprint as sha256_text of the CanonicalJsonWriter serialization of the shipped entry document, BARE 64 hex, pinned by a length-64 assertion, on the grounds that it follows the four precedent fingerprint sites and Task 6 finding I-4. That was an IMPLEMENTER decision taken with stated rationale rather than a maintainer ruling, and DEVIATION-14 itself instructs the next implementer to re-derive its findings at source.

WHAT WAS MEASURED AT SOURCE THIS SESSION, WHICH DECISION 2 MISSED. A producer for exactly that value ALREADY SHIPS and is already law. scripts/narrative/DialogicEntryManifest.gd:392 declares static func fingerprint(document: Dictionary) -> String, which is CanonicalJsonWriter.stringify then HashingContext SHA-256 over the canonical UTF-8 bytes - the same algorithm decision 2 specifies - and returns "sha256:" plus the lowercase hex. It is one of exactly four public statics named in DECLARED_METHOD_NAMES at tests/unit/test_dialogic_entry_manifest.gd:303, and two GREEN tests in the FROZEN four-dialogic-unit baseline pin it: :1728-1729 assert it begins with "sha256:" and is exactly 71 characters, and :1741-1754 recompute the SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of the REAL shipped 85428-byte document independently and assert equality. It is additionally proven deterministic, content-sensitive and RECORD-ORDER-sensitive at :1719-1738. So CanonicalJsonWriter demonstrably round-trips the real 139-record document today; that is not an assumption.

THE DISPOSITION. Task 7 uses DialogicEntryManifest.fingerprint(document) verbatim. manifest_fingerprint is the "sha256:"-prefixed 71-character form, pinned by a begins_with("sha256:") plus length-71 assertion rather than the length-64 one decision 2 named.

RATIONALE. Decision 2 would have created a SECOND, differently formatted digest of the SAME document beside a shipped one, so two fingerprints of one document could be compared against each other and silently never match. That is precisely the divergence Ruling 14-A's own rationale exists to prevent, applied to the manifest instead of to the resolution law. The prefixed form is also this participant's EXISTING fingerprint vocabulary: NarrativeRestoreParticipant already compares content_fingerprint values that are "sha256:"-prefixed, and both suites fixture them that way (tests/integration/test_dialogic_restore.gd:12 and tests/integration/test_restore_production_adapters.gd:228).

THE ONE ARGUMENT AGAINST, RECORDED HONESTLY. Bare sha256_text hex is the repository's dominant convention at 30-plus sites, and DialogicEntryManifest.fingerprint is the single prefixed outlier. That was measured, weighed and overruled: reusing one tested producer beats matching a formatting convention with a second definition of the same value.

DIGEST AND BASELINE IMPACT: NONE. No plan byte changes, so the roadmap Plan Digest Manifest and implementation_plan_sha256 stay exact. DialogicEntryManifest.gd is NOT edited, so the frozen four-dialogic-unit baseline 4/242/242/11631 is untouched, and DialogicEntryManifest.gd is bound in no evidence artifact.

CARRY-FORWARD. Plan 04 stores manifest_fingerprint per receipt alongside a separate signature_hash; it inherits this spelling.

RULING 15-B (THE STANDING-PLAYBACK REFUSAL MOVES TO apply_silent, WIDENING RULING 14-A's GRANT FROM ONE NEW PUBLIC BRIDGE ENTRY TO TWO). MAINTAINER-RATIFIED 2026-09-01 via AskUserQuestion during Task 7 implementation, recorded in the session that obtained it. Raised by the ONE FRESH REVIEWER as finding M-3 and VERIFIED AT SOURCE before the question was put, not accepted on the reviewer's word.

WHAT THE TASK 7 BRIEF DIRECTED. entry_already_active was DELIBERATELY excluded from validate_resume_checkpoint, on the ground that activity is a transient runtime precondition rather than a compatibility property of the save, so prepare must not reject a compatible bundle because playback happens to be live. The consequence was to be "stated as a law instead": an active entry at finalize returns the bridge's refusal envelope unchanged and substitutes nothing.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. autoload/SaveManager.gd runs the apply_silent loop at :639-677, where a participant refusal at :644-646 rolls back BEFORE anything durable happens. It then commits the checkpoint journal at :680 - _journal.commit_prepared - and only afterwards runs the finalize loop at :686-689, where a refusal at :689 rolls back AFTER that commit. So the ONE precondition excluded from the validator is exactly the one whose refusal lands past the point of no return. That is, verbatim, the hazard Ruling 14-A's own rationale exists to prevent: "a restore that passes prepare, commits the checkpoint journal, and then fails inside finalize after the transaction is already past its rollback point." A live semantic entry or a live ending playback is a realistic state when a player loads a save mid-conversation, and _begin_entry_playback guards on _active_entry OR _active_playback, so both vocabularies reach it.

THE DISPOSITION. validate_resume_checkpoint stays PURE and activity-blind exactly as directed, so a compatible bundle is still never rejected at prepare time for a transient runtime state. The refusal moves to NarrativeRestoreParticipant.apply_silent, the last hook before the commit, where SaveManager's own apply-loop rollback is the designed path. The participant needs to ask the bridge whether any playback is standing, and NO existing public entry answers that: get_current_timeline_id and get_current_narrative_checkpoint read the LEGACY _current_timeline_id, not _active_entry or _active_playback, and abort_current_entry mutates. So Task 7 adds a SECOND new column-zero public entry, has_active_playback() -> bool, a pure read that starts, stops, clears and mutates nothing.

DECLARED COST, to be checked against the observed gate and never assumed: the tooling assert figure moves 14395 to 14396, one per new public entry under the plus-one rule DEVIATION-14 proved by historical control, and NOTHING else moves beyond the two test families Task 7 already declared. The desktop handoff re-seal is regenerated once more in the same commit; it was already owed.

THE COST WAS STATED BEFORE THE CHOICE, NOT DISCOVERED AFTER IT. The option the maintainer selected carried the explicit note that choosing it means widening 14-A by one entry.

BOTH OPERANDS OF THE NEW GUARD ARE PINNED, because has_active_playback is a two-operand predicate over _active_entry and _active_playback and a one-sided fixture would leave a guaranteed survivor. _begin_entry_playback is refactored to call it too, so the one-active-playback law has ONE copy rather than two.

REJECTED, WITH THE REASON RECORDED. Leaving the refusal at finalize as the brief directed. It is not unsafe - _rollback_transaction restores every participant from its captured backup, so the outcome is a refused restore rather than a corrupted one - and it would have kept 14-A's grant intact at 14395. It was rejected because a refusal that forces a rollback of an already-committed journal is strictly worse than one that never commits, and because the whole purpose of the validator seam is that prepare and finalize cannot disagree.

CARRY-FORWARD. The 14.4 cross-store transaction journal remains owned by Plan 04 under Ruling 14-C; this ruling does not reach into it and changes no journal byte.

WHY CLOSING IS MECHANICALLY CLEAN. bd open-children refusal is epic-only: cmd/bd/close.go:123 is "if !force && issue != nil && issue.IssueType == types.TypeEpic", and its message is the only open-children string in the resolved bd.exe. dwm-oyo.2 is issue_type task, so that guard cannot fire. The second guard at close.go:140-149 refuses a close when the issue is itself blocked; dwm-oyo.2 does not appear in bd blocked, its only dependency dwm-oyo.1 being closed. A third check, validateIssueClosable at close.go:117, is only NotTemplate plus NotPinned and contains no children test.

THE PRECEDENT CLAIM WAS OVERTURNED, AND THE CORRECTED FORM SUPPORTS THIS RULING. The first measurement asserted that no parent in this database has ever been closed over an open child. That is true only of the current snapshot, not of the history. dwm-p2r.35, a bug parent of eight, was closed 2026-08-24T08:40:58Z while its child dwm-p2r.35.8, created 2026-08-24T01:39:50Z, was still open; the parent close reason ends ".35.8 deliberately deferred, follow-ups on dwm-p2r.36". That child was then STARTED at 08:48:27Z, seven and a half minutes AFTER its parent closed, and closed at 09:42:14Z. So closing a non-epic parent over an open child, deliberately and with a written rationale, and then continuing to work that child, is exactly precedented in this database.

THE DOMINANT CONSEQUENCE IS THE UNBLOCK, NOT THE COSMETICS. dwm-oyo.3, .4, .5, .6 and .7 each carry a blocks edge on dwm-oyo.2, and bd blocked lists all five. dwm-oyo.3 is blocked by dwm-oyo.2 ALONE - its other prerequisites dwm-oyo.1 and dwm-p2r.9 are both closed - so this close makes dwm-oyo.3 ready and cascades onward. Leaving dwm-oyo.2 in_progress would have kept all five downstream phases blocked while its acceptance criterion was already satisfied, which is a false statement of state.

WHY REPARENT RATHER THAN LEAVE OR DETACH. bd tree rendering promotes the children of a closed parent to top level: bd list --tree showed dwm-oyo.2.1 and dwm-oyo.2.2 flat and alphabetically interleaved among genuine roots with no parent displayed. Reparenting to dwm-oyo keeps both debts visible AND makes them binding, because the epic guard requires every child closed before an epic can close, and this repository already states that law for itself in prose and in code: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-11-desktop-minesweeper-shop-schedule-04-verification-closeout.md:181 orders proving every child closed before closing the epic, and tools/evidence/Phase2RCloseoutInventory.gd:274-276 fails with code class_member_open when a named non-contract child is not closed. Detaching to standalone, the dwm-6wa precedent, was rejected because it drops the Phase 01 provenance link.

NOTHING IS LOST BY CLOSING. Both children keep their own ids, descriptions, acceptance criteria and comment histories. dwm-oyo.2.1 already names a deferred owner in its own text - close it in whichever later task first designs that seam, and add a campaign site proving the mutant then dies - and dwm-oyo.2.2 keeps ownership on itself under DEVIATION-11 Ruling B and states that none is blocking. BLOCKED-STATE NOTE, MEASURED. is_blocked does propagate down parent-child edges (internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go:141-182), so the reparent was checked afterwards rather than assumed: dwm-oyo is not itself blocked, and both children were confirmed still unblocked after reparenting.

THE DESCRIPTION IS DISCHARGED AT TASK GRANULARITY, NOT AT WORK-ITEM GRANULARITY, AND THAT IS RECORDED HONESTLY. Plan 01 defines exactly SEVEN Tasks (headings at plan lines 38, 85, 169, 238, 268, 313, 347) plus the trailing Phase 01 Verification Gate at line 380 with its eight bullets, and the 389-line file ends inside that bullet list. RULING 17-B (SEVEN-DAY PLAN 02 OWNERSHIP). Plan 02 was GENUINELY RECONCILED. No bead is missing for the slot: dwm-oyo.3 IS the Plan 02 bead. One bead is filed for the measured residue. Full evidence is recorded on dwm-oyo.3; the summary is that the dwm-oyo.3 original registered record was titled "Phase 02 - Calendar contacts schedule and Hospital" and its description named the Plan 02 file, and the 2026-08-11 amendment roadmap line 79 supersedes Plan 02 into that roadmap Plan 03, which owns the same Bead.
